name: Antigua and Barbuda
motto: Each Endeavouring, All Achieving
climate: Tropical maritime with little seasonal temperature variation; dry season from January to April
naturalHazards: Hurricanes and tropical storms (Atlantic hurricane season)
environmentalIssues: Freshwater scarcity requiring major seawater reverse-osmosis desalination
biodiversity: Home to 365 white and pink sand beaches, Great Bird Island (sanctuary for the rare Antiguan racer snake), and the Frigate Bird Sanctuary in Barbuda
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Sir Rodney Williams)
latestElections: General election 2023; general election scheduled 2028
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Gaston Browne leading national economic expansion; hosted the 4th UN International Conference on Small Island Developing States (SIDS4) in St. John's in 2024.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; leading global advocate for climate loss and damage compensation for island states.
military: Antigua and Barbuda Defence Force (ABDF: 1st Battalion Antigua and Barbuda Regiment, Coast Guard).
adminDivisions: 6 parishes on Antigua, and 2 dependencies (Barbuda and Redonda)
history: Inhabited by the Siboney and later Arawak and Carib peoples. Christopher Columbus sighted the island in 1493, naming it Santa María de la Antigua. Colonized by Britain in 1632, establishing immense sugarcane plantations powered by enslaved Africans. Admiral Horatio Nelson established Nelson's Dockyard in English Harbour in the 18th century as the Royal Navy's chief Caribbean base. Gained full independence on November 1, 1981 under Sir Vere Cornwall Bird.
recentEvents2020_2026: Hosted the United Nations SIDS4 global conference in May 2024; completed modern cruise pier expansions in St. John's harbor; led international tribunal initiatives on ocean climate law.
historicalFigures: Sir Vere Cornwall Bird (Father of the Nation)
King Court (Prince Klaas, 1736 slave resistance leader)
religions: Christianity (Anglican ~18%, Seventh-day Adventist ~12%, Pentecostal ~12%, Moravian ~8%, Roman Catholic ~8%, Methodist ~6%) ~77%
education: University of the West Indies (UWI) Five Islands Campus, American University of Antigua (AUA College of Medicine); free compulsory schooling.
healthcare: Sir Lester Bird Mount St. John's Medical Centre in St. John's provides advanced regional medical care.
socialCustoms: Lively Sunday cricket matches, Shirley Heights sunset steelband barbecues, Carnival masquerade jumping.
etiquette: Friendly and respectful, polite 'Good morning' or 'Good afternoon' greetings, church modesty.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the legendary 365 beaches, world sailing heritage in English Harbour, cricket royalty, and vibrant calypso rhythms.
sectors: Tourism & Hospitality 60%, Financial Services & Commerce 25%, Construction 10%, Agriculture & Fisheries 5%
naturalResources: Pristine coral beaches and natural harbors
energy: Over 25% solar energy penetration through expanding utility-scale PV installations, backed by modern fuel generators
tourism: Over 1.1 million total cruise and stayover visitors enjoying Nelson's Dockyard (UNESCO World Heritage Site), Shirley Heights, Dickenson Bay, and Barbuda pink sand beaches.
employment: Unemployment approx. 6.8%; major employment in hospitality, international yachting, and financial services.
debtInflation: Stable monetary regime pegged to the US Dollar ($1 USD = $2.70 XCD) managed by the Eastern Caribbean Central Bank (ECCB).
transport: Paved road network across Antigua; regular passenger ferry and air charters connecting Antigua and Barbuda.
airports: V.C. Bird International Airport (ANU on Antigua - modern regional hub)
ports: Heritage Quay and Point Wharf (St. John's Deepwater Harbour)
English Harbour & Falmouth Harbour (premier Caribbean superyacht hubs)
cuisine: Fungee and Pepperpot (national dish: cornmeal okra dumpling served with rich meat stew), Ducana (sweet potato dumplings steamed in banana leaves), Fresh Barbuda spiny lobster, Saltfish, Johnny cakes, English Harbour rum.
festivals: Antigua Carnival (celebrating emancipation in late July/August)
Antigua Sailing Week (world-renowned international regatta)
Independence Food Fair
music: Calypso, Soca, Steelband pan music, Reggae, Zouk.
dance: Carnival masquerade chip and wine, Benna folk dance.
art: Vibrant Caribbean acrylic seascapes, pottery from Sea View Farm, hand-woven palm hats.
architecture: Georgian naval brick and stone architecture of Nelson's Dockyard; St. John's Cathedral (baroque twin-towered wooden interior); colorful gingerbread chattel houses.
literature: Jamaica Kincaid (acclaimed novelist: A Small Place, Annie John, Lucy), Althea Prince.
cinema: Filming location for international sailing documentaries and travel features.
sports: Cricket (home of legendary master blaster Sir Vivian Richards, Sir Curtly Ambrose, and Sir Andy Roberts; Sir Vivian Richards Stadium), Sailing, Football.
media: Antigua Observer, Pointe Xpress, ABS TV & Radio.
clothing: Traditional national costume in madras plaid pattern with white apron and headwrap; smart casual island wear.
crafts: Sea View Farm traditional clay coal pots, shell jewelry, carved mahogany crafts.
worldHeritageSites: Antigua Naval Dockyard and Related Archaeological Sites (Nelson's Dockyard)
unescoIntangible: Antigua Carnival and steelband musical heritage
flagDescription: Red field with an inverted V-shape containing horizontal bands of black, light blue, and white, with a rising golden seven-pointed sun centered on the black band.
coatOfArmsDescription: A shield supported by two deer depicting a rising sun over a blue and white sea with a sugar mill on land, topped by an ornate helmet and pineapple, above the banner 'EACH ENDEAVOURING, ALL ACHIEVING'.
travelNotes: Celebrated as 'the beach is just the beginning'; safe, sunny, world-class sailing and luxury resort paradise.
shortSummary: Antigua and Barbuda is a twin-island Caribbean gem famed for its 365 sun-drenched beaches, the historic Georgian naval fortress of Nelson's Dockyard, and an illustrious legacy of cricket titans.
sources: Statistics Division of Antigua and Barbuda

name: Bahamas
motto: Forward, Upward, Onward, Together
highestPoint: Mount Alvernia on Cat Island (63 m)
climate: Tropical marine with pleasant trade winds; mild winters and warm summers; hurricane season from June to November
naturalHazards: Major hurricanes and coastal storm surges (e.g., Hurricane Dorian)
environmentalIssues: Solid waste management on Out Islands
biodiversity: Archipelago of 700 islands and 2,400 cays stretching over 800 km; world's third longest barrier reef (Andros Barrier Reef) and Inagua National Park (world's largest colony of West Indian flamingos)
currency: Bahamian Dollar (BSD, B$ - pegged 1:1 with USD)
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Dame Cynthia A. Pratt)
legislature: Parliament of the Bahamas (Senate and House of Assembly)
latestElections: General election 2021; general election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Philip Davis leading national focus on climate finance, blue carbon credit monetization, renewable energy expansion across family islands, and economic diversification.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; close diplomatic and economic alliance with the United States.
military: Royal Bahamas Defence Force (RBDF: all-naval coast guard force including maritime patrol, air wing, and commando squadron).
adminDivisions: 32 local government districts (across New Providence and the Family Islands)
history: Inhabited by the peaceful Lucayan Taíno people for over 600 years. Christopher Columbus made his momentous first landfall in the Americas on the Bahamian island of Guanahani (San Salvador) on October 12, 1492. Colonized by English Eleutheran Adventurers seeking religious freedom in 1648. Nassau became the notorious pirate capital of the 'Republic of Pirates' (Blackbeard, Calico Jack, Charles Vane) until Royal Governor Woodes Rogers restored order in 1718 under the motto 'Expulsis Piratis Restituta Commercia'. Gained independence from Britain on July 10, 1973 under Sir Lynden Pindling.
recentEvents2020_2026: Achieved record tourism arrivals surpassing 9.5 million visitors; launched the Bahamas Blue Carbon Initiative trading marine credits; held major regional CARICOM summits in Nassau.
historicalFigures: Sir Lynden Pindling (Father of the Nation)
religions: Protestant (Baptist ~35%, Anglican ~14%, Pentecostal ~9%, Seventh-day Adventist ~4%, Methodist ~4%) ~70%
education: University of The Bahamas (UB in Nassau) and Eugene Dupuch Law School; free public primary and secondary education.
healthcare: Princess Margaret Hospital in Nassau and Rand Memorial Hospital in Freeport provide comprehensive public medical care.
socialCustoms: Junkanoo street parades (Boxing Day and New Year's Day), Friday fish fries at Arawak Cay, Sunday family dinners with peas 'n rice.
etiquette: Polite greeting with formal titles ('Mr./Mrs.'), warm hospitality, respectful attitude in civic spaces.
nationalIdentity: Defined by turquoise waters so clear they are visible from space, vibrant Junkanoo rhythms, world-class banking, and maritime excellence.
gdpPerCapita: $34,900 (one of the highest in the Americas)
sectors: Tourism & Hospitality 55%, Financial & Professional Services 20%, Construction & Real Estate 15%, Agriculture & Fisheries 10%
industries: Offshore private banking and trust management
Ship registry (one of world's largest open ship registries)
naturalResources: Pristine coral reefs and turquoise ocean waters
energy: Historically heavy fuel oil; transitioning to utility-scale solar PV microgrids across the Family Islands
tourism: Over 9.5 million cruise and stopover visitors enjoying Atlantis Paradise Island, Baha Mar, swimming with pigs in Exuma, diving the Andros Barrier Reef, and Harbour Island pink sands.
employment: High employment in tourism, financial compliance, maritime operations, and aviation.
debtInflation: Bahamian Dollar firmly pegged 1:1 to the US Dollar backed by the Central Bank of The Bahamas; stable macroeconomic environment.
transport: Extensive inter-island mailboat ferry network; New Providence highway system; major international cruise port terminals.
airports: Lynden Pindling International Airport (NAS in Nassau - with US border pre-clearance)
ports: Nassau Cruise Port (recently transformed $300M modern terminal handling 30,000+ cruise passengers daily)
cuisine: Conch salad (fresh diced conch with lime juice, orange, peppers, and onions), Cracked conch, Bahamian rock lobster, Peas 'n rice, Guava duff (traditional rolled sponge dessert with warm rum butter sauce), Goombay Smash and Bahama Mama cocktails.
festivals: Junkanoo (spectacular boxing day and new year's street parades featuring towering crepe-paper costumes and cowbell beats)
Bahamas International Film Festival
Regattas (National Family Island Regatta in Exuma)
music: Junkanoo brass and goat-skin drumming, Rake 'n' Scrape (accordion, saw, and goatskin drum), Goombay, Calypso.
dance: Junkanoo rush-out dance, Quadrille, Limbo.
art: Amos Ferguson (visionary folk painter), Brent Malone, Antonius Roberts, National Art Gallery of The Bahamas (NAGB).
architecture: Colonial pastel-colored buildings with louvred wooden shutters in Nassau, Government House, historic Fort Fincastle and Queen's Staircase.
literature: Sir Etienne Dupuch, Robert Johnson, Marion Bethel, Patricia Glinton-Meicholas.
cinema: Famous filming destination for James Bond films (Thunderball, Casino Royale), Pirates of the Caribbean, Splash.
sports: Track and field (Olympic Gold medalists: Shaunae Miller-Uibo, Steven Gardiner, Golden Girls), Basketball (NBA stars Buddy Hield, Deandre Ayton), Sailing (native sloop regattas).
media: The Tribune, The Nassau Guardian, ZNS Bahamas (Broadcasting Corporation of The Bahamas), Eyewitness News.
clothing: Traditional colorful Junkanoo crepe-paper costumes; breezy tropical resort wear; Androsia hand-waxed batik fabrics.
crafts: Hand-woven straw work (Nassau Straw Market: hats, bags, mats), Androsia batik cloth, conch shell carvings.
worldHeritageSites: Tentative List: Historic Forts of Nassau, Inagua National Park, Central Andros Marine Parks
unescoIntangible: Junkanoo festival traditions and craftsmanship (inscribed on UNESCO Representative List 2023)
famousPeople: Sir Sidney Poitier (first Black actor to win Best Actor Oscar, raised in Bahamas)
flagDescription: Black equilateral triangle based on the hoist side pointing toward three equal horizontal stripes of aquamarine (top and bottom, representing the turquoise seas) and gold (center, representing the sunny shores).
coatOfArmsDescription: A shield showing Christopher Columbus's flagship Santa María sailing under a rising sun, supported by a blue marlin and a flamingo, topped by a pink conch shell, with the motto 'FORWARD, UPWARD, ONWARD, TOGETHER'.
landmarks: Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park (Swimming Pigs)
Dean's Blue Hole (world's second deepest blue hole on Long Island at 202m)
travelNotes: Premier luxury travel haven; crystal-clear marine waters; direct flights from major international hubs; US dollars accepted 1:1 everywhere.
shortSummary: The Bahamas is an archipelago of 700 sun-drenched islands boasting the clearest waters on Earth, vibrant Junkanoo rhythms, historic pirate havens, and legendary marine wonders from the Exuma swimming pigs to pink sand shores.

name: Barbados
nationalAnthem: In Plenty and In Time of Need
motto: Pride and Industry
climate: Tropical maritime with pleasant trade winds; dry season from December to May; rainy season from June to November
naturalHazards: Tropical cyclones and hurricanes (situated south of primary Caribbean hurricane belt)
biodiversity: Non-volcanic coral limestone island featuring Harrison's Cave stalactites, lush botanical gardens, and nesting hawksbill sea turtles
currency: Barbadian Dollar (BBD, Bds$ - pegged 2:1 with USD)
legislature: Parliament of Barbados (Senate and House of Assembly)
latestElections: General election 2022 (BLP won all 30 parliamentary seats); general election scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Mia Mottley leading the globally recognized 'Bridgetown Initiative' reforming international climate finance and multilateral development banking; republican institutional consolidation.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; global leader in global financial architecture reform, climate resilience, and reparations advocacy.
military: Barbados Defence Force (BDF: Barbados Regiment, Barbados Coast Guard).
history: Inhabited by Amerindian Saladoid-Barrancoid, Arawak, and Carib peoples. Portuguese sailors named it Os Barbados ('The Bearded Ones') after bearded fig trees. British settlement began at Holetown in 1627. Barbados became the premier sugar-producing colony in the British Empire powered by enslaved Africans, establishing the world's oldest continuous rum distillery (Mount Gay Rum, 1703). Gained independence in 1966 under Errol Barrow. On November 30, 2021, Barbados removed Queen Elizabeth II as head of state, becoming a republic while appointing global superstar Rihanna as National Hero.
recentEvents2020_2026: Championed the Bridgetown Initiative at COP28 and global climate summits; elected to international leadership forums; hosted the ICC Men's T20 Cricket World Cup Final in Kensington Oval in June 2024.
religions: Protestant (Anglican ~24%, Pentecostal ~11%, Seventh-day Adventist ~6%, Methodist ~4%, Baptist ~3%) ~66%
literacyRate: 99.6% (one of the highest in the Americas)
education: University of the West Indies (UWI) Cave Hill Campus; world-class free public primary, secondary, and tertiary education.
healthcare: Queen Elizabeth Hospital in Bridgetown provides tertiary medical care; extensive network of free public polyclinics.
socialCustoms: Friday night fish fry in Oistins, Crop Over festival grand kadooment carnival jumping, passionate cricket debates at rum shops.
etiquette: Courteous, British-influenced manners, addressing elders with respect, smart casual attire in commercial establishments.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated for 'Bajan' pride, high educational attainment, rich rum distillation heritage, cricket genius, and the global cultural impact of Rihanna.
sectors: Services & Tourism 68%, Finance & Business 18%, Light Manufacturing & Rum 9%, Agriculture 5%
industries: International business and offshore financial services
Rum distilling (Mount Gay, Foursquare, St. Nicholas Abbey)
Information technology and digital nomad visas ('Barbados Welcome Stamp')
agriculture: Vegetables and root crops (yams, sweet potatoes)
energy: Aggressive transition toward 100% renewable electricity by 2030 led by utility-scale solar PV and wind energy
exports: Premium rum (world's oldest commercial rum brands)
tourism: Over 1.4 million stayover and cruise visitors enjoying the Platinum Coast (St. James luxury resorts), Bathsheba surf breaks (Soup Bowl), Harrison's Cave, and Kensington Oval.
employment: High literacy and skilled service employment across tourism, banking, law, and renewable energy.
debtInflation: Barbadian Dollar pegged 2:1 with the US Dollar since 1975; strong international credit ratings supported by IMF Extended Fund Facility.
transport: Dense paved road network across all 11 parishes; modern electric public bus fleet (Transport Board); Bridgetown cruise and cargo port.
airports: Grantley Adams International Airport (BGI - major Eastern Caribbean aviation hub)
ports: Port of Bridgetown (deepwater cruise and container terminal)
cuisine: Cou-cou and Flying Fish (national dish: cornmeal and okra paste served with steamed flying fish in rich tomato-onion-thyme gravy), Fish cakes with Bajan pepper sauce, Macaroni pie, Pudding and souse (pickled pork with steamed sweet potato), Mount Gay Rum punch.
festivals: Crop Over Festival (centuries-old harvest festival culminating in Grand Kadooment carnival in August)
Oistins Fish Festival (Easter weekend)
Barbados Food and Rum Festival
music: Soca, Calypso, Tuk band music (bass drum, snare drum, triangle, and penny whistle), Spouge (indigenous genre created by Jackie Opel), Reggae.
dance: Kadooment carnival dancing, Tuk band masquerade (Mother Sally, Shaggy Bear).
art: Vibrant visual arts tradition, wood carvings, pottery from Chalky Mount, Barbados Museum and Historical Society.
architecture: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison (UNESCO World Heritage Site); Jacobean mansions (St. Nicholas Abbey, Drax Hall); traditional wooden Chattel houses.
literature: Kamau Brathwaite (master poet and Caribbean thinker), George Lamming (In the Castle of My Skin), Austin Clarke.
cinema: Filming location for international Caribbean features and world-class surfing documentaries at the Soup Bowl.
sports: Cricket (the national sport; Kensington Oval is known as the 'Mecca of Cricket'; home to legendary Sir Garfield Sobers, Sir Frank Worrell, Sir Everton Weekes, Sir Clyde Walcott), Surfing, Road Tennis (indigenous racquet sport invented in Barbados in the 1930s).
media: The Daily Nation, The Barbados Advocate, CBC TV 8 (Caribbean Broadcasting Corporation), Starcom Network.
clothing: Smart casual attire; vibrant Crop Over carnival feathered regalia; beachwear restricted to beaches and pools.
crafts: Chalky Mount red clay pottery, woven pandanus and palm hats, mahogany carvings.
worldHeritageSites: Historic Bridgetown and its Garrison (UNESCO World Heritage Site designated in 2011)
unescoIntangible: Crop Over Festival traditions and Tuk Band musical heritage
famousPeople: Robyn Rihanna Fenty (Pop icon, billionaire entrepreneur, and National Hero of Barbados)
Grandmaster Flash (Bajan heritage hip hop pioneer)
flagDescription: Triband of three equal vertical stripes of ultramarine blue (ocean and sky), gold (sandy beaches), and ultramarine blue, charged with a black broken trident head centered on the gold stripe (symbolizing independence and break from British colonial rule).
coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by a dolphin fish (mahi-mahi) and a pelican, displaying a bearded fig tree and two pride of Barbados flowers, topped by an arm holding two crossed sugarcane stalks, with the motto 'PRIDE AND INDUSTRY'.
travelNotes: One of the safest, most stable, and sophisticated destinations in the Caribbean; warm Bajan hospitality; excellent dining and heritage.
shortSummary: Barbados is a sophisticated coral island republic in the Eastern Caribbean, celebrated as the birthplace of rum, home to the UNESCO-listed Garrison of Bridgetown, the cradle of cricket legends, and the homeland of global icon Rihanna.

name: Belize
motto: Sub Umbra Floreo (Under the Shade I Flourish)
climate: Tropical rainy with wet season May to November
biodiversity: Home to Belize Barrier Reef (second largest in world) and Cockscomb Basin Wildlife Sanctuary (world's first jaguar preserve)
currency: Belize Dollar (BZD, BZ$ - pegged 2:1 with USD)
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Dame Froyla Tzalam)
legislature: National Assembly (Senate and House of Representatives)
latestElections: General election 2020; municipal 2024; general election 2025
politicalSituation: Pioneering blue bond debt-for-nature swap protecting the Belize Barrier Reef; border dispute arbitration before ICJ.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, SICA, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; diplomatic ties with Taiwan.
military: Belize Defence Force (BDF).
history: Heartland of the ancient Maya civilization (Caracol, Xunantunich, Lamanai). English buccaneers (Baymen) settled in the 17th century to cut logwood. Battle of St. George's Caye (1798) cemented British control over Spanish claims. Known as British Honduras until 1973. Achieved independence on September 21, 1981 under George Cadle Price.
recentEvents2020_2026: Expanded marine protected areas under landmark Blue Bond refinancing; progressed International Court of Justice territorial hearings with Guatemala.
historicalFigures: George Cadle Price (Father of the Nation)
education: University of Belize (UB in Belmopan and Belize City); bilingual education programs.
healthcare: Karl Heusner Memorial Hospital (KHMH in Belize City) and regional hospitals.
socialCustoms: Garifuna Settlement Day celebrations, Punta dancing, Belizean Kriol storytelling, Sunday rice and beans.
etiquette: Friendly and laid-back, polite greetings, respect for indigenous Mayan and Garifuna customs.
nationalIdentity: Unique bridge between Central America and the Caribbean, combining ancient Maya pyramids, Garifuna drumming, and pristine coral cayes.
energy: Over 50% renewable: Hydroelectric (Chalillo, Mollejon), Biomass (bagasse), backed by Mexico grid imports
tourism: Over 1.7 million visitors enjoying the Great Blue Hole, Ambergris Caye, Caye Caulker, Xunantunich, and Actun Tunichil Muknal (ATM) Cave.
employment: Tourism and hospitality, agro-industry, public administration.
debtInflation: BZD pegged 2:1 to USD; public debt reduced via Blue Bond transaction.
transport: George Price Highway and Philip Goldson Highway; water taxis connecting cayes.
airports: Philip S.W. Goldson International (BZE in Ladyville/Belize City)
ports: Big Creek Port (banana and citrus export terminal)
cuisine: Rice and beans cooked in coconut milk with stewed chicken, Fry jacks with refried beans, Hudut (Garifuna fish stew with plantain), Conch fritters, Marie Sharp's habanero pepper sauce.
festivals: September Celebrations (Battle of St. George's Caye and Independence Day)
Garifuna Settlement Day (November 19)
San Pedro Lobster Festival
music: Punta Rock (created by Andy Palacio), Garifuna drumming, Brukdown, Reggae, Soca.
dance: Punta dance, Wanaragua (John Canoe dance).
art: Slate carvings by Maya artisans, Ziricote wood carvings, vibrant Garifuna paintings by Pen Cayetano.
architecture: Ancient Maya limestone temples (El Castillo at Xunantunich, Caana at Caracol); colonial timber houses on stilts.
literature: Zee Edgell (Beka Lamb - landmark novel of Belizean literature), Evan X Hyde.
cinema: Filming setting for The Dogs of War; celebrated environmental and archaeological documentaries.
sports: Cycling (Holy Saturday Cross Country Cycling Classic), Football, Basketball, Softball.
media: Amandala, The Reporter, Channel 5 (Great Belize Television), Channel 7.
clothing: Casual tropical attire; colorful Garifuna yellow, black, and white traditional attire during festivities.
crafts: Carved Mayan slate glyphs, Ziricote wood crafts, woven Jippi Jappa baskets.
worldHeritageSites: Belize Barrier Reef Reserve System (including the Great Blue Hole and seven protected marine areas)
unescoIntangible: Language, dance and music of the Garifuna (inscribed 2008)
flagDescription: Royal blue field with narrow red stripes at top and bottom, centered with a white disc bearing the coat of arms featuring two woodcutters (one Mestizo, one Creole) flanked by a mahogany tree.
coatOfArmsDescription: Shield partitioned into tools of the logging industry (paddle, axes, saw), supported by two woodsmen beneath a mahogany tree, over the motto 'SUB UMBRA FLOREO'.
landmarks: Ambergris Caye & Hol Chan Marine Reserve
travelNotes: English-speaking Central American paradise; world-class scuba diving, snorkeling, and rainforest caving.
shortSummary: Belize is a captivating crossroads of Caribbean culture and ancient Maya heritage, home to the second-largest barrier reef on Earth, the mysterious Great Blue Hole, and lush jaguar-filled rainforests.

name: Canada
motto: A Mari Usque Ad Mare (From Sea to Sea)
longestRiver: Mackenzie River (4,241 km) / St. Lawrence River
climate: Subarctic and arctic across north, continental with warm summers and cold snowy winters in south, oceanic temperate on Pacific coast
naturalHazards: Severe winter blizzards and ice storms
biodiversity: Vast intact boreal forests, Arctic tundra, Pacific coastal rainforests; habitat for grizzly bears, polar bears, moose, and caribou
timeZone: UTC-08:00 to UTC-03:30 (six time zones across 5,500 km)
languages: French (both official; French predominant in Quebec)
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor General Mary Simon - first Indigenous Governor General)
legislature: Parliament of Canada (Senate and House of Commons)
constitution: 1867 (Constitution Act, patriated 1982 with Charter of Rights and Freedoms)
latestElections: Federal election 2021; federal general election scheduled 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Focus on critical mineral supply chains, housing affordability, clean tech transition, and Arctic sovereignty.
foreignRelations: Member of G7, G20, NATO, Five Eyes, USMCA, Commonwealth, Francophonie, OECD, UN; champion of rules-based multilateralism.
military: Canadian Armed Forces (CAF: Canadian Army, Royal Canadian Navy, Royal Canadian Air Force) and NORAD partner.
history: Inhabited for over 15,000 years by First Nations and Inuit peoples. Norse settlement at L'Anse aux Meadows around 1000 CE. French explorer Jacques Cartier mapped the St. Lawrence in 1534; Samuel de Champlain founded Quebec in 1608. Britain gained control after the Seven Years' War (Treaty of Paris 1763). Confederation established on July 1, 1867. Canadian forces forged national identity at Vimy Ridge in WWI. Canada patriated its constitution with the Charter of Rights and Freedoms in 1982.
recentEvents2020_2026: Accelerated critical mineral agreements for electric vehicles with US and European allies; advanced Indigenous reconciliation and self-governance; hosted G7 ministerial sessions.
historicalFigures: Lester B. Pearson (Nobel Peace Prize winner)
education: World-class university institutions led by University of Toronto, McGill University, UBC, and University of Alberta; high OECD PISA education rankings.
healthcare: Medicare universal, publicly funded healthcare system providing medically necessary hospital and physician services free at the point of delivery.
socialCustoms: Deep passion for ice hockey, multicultural inclusiveness, apologizing politely ('sorry'), enjoying maple syrup tapping in spring sugar shacks.
etiquette: Polite, modest, punctual, respectful of diversity, queue-conscious, firm handshake.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the vast northern wilderness, bilingual mosaic, universal healthcare, peacekeeping heritage, and hockey excellence.
energy: Over 82% clean electricity: Hydroelectric (60%), Nuclear (15%), Wind and solar (7%), Natural gas and coal (18%)
tourism: Over 22 million international visitors exploring Banff and Jasper National Parks in the Rockies, Niagara Falls, CN Tower, Old Quebec, and Vancouver.
employment: Unemployment approx. 6.2%; high immigration targets bringing skilled global talent.
debtInflation: AAA sovereign rating; Bank of Canada maintains inflation near 2% target.
transport: Trans-Canada Highway (7,821 km); transcontinental freight railways (CN and CPKC); St. Lawrence Seaway.
cuisine: Poutine (crispy fries with fresh cheese curds and rich brown gravy), Tourtière (Quebec spiced meat pie), Montreal smoked meat, Butter tarts, Nanaimo bars, Canadian wild smoked salmon, Maple syrup.
festivals: Montreal International Jazz Festival (world's largest)
Calgary Stampede ('The Greatest Outdoor Show on Earth')
Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF)
Winterlude (Ottawa)
Quebec Winter Carnival
music: Global superstars (Céline Dion, Drake, The Weeknd, Justin Bieber, Joni Mitchell, Neil Young, Leonard Cohen, Rush, Shania Twain), classical virtuosos (Glenn Gould).
dance: The National Ballet of Canada, Les Grands Ballets Canadiens, Indigenous powwow dances.
art: Group of Seven landscape painters (Tom Thomson, Lawren Harris), Emily Carr, Norval Morrisseau (Woodland Style), Inuit soapstone carvings.
architecture: Château-style grand railway hotels (Château Frontenac, Banff Springs Hotel), iconic CN Tower, Canadian Museum of History (Douglas Cardinal design).
literature: Margaret Atwood (The Handmaid's Tale), Alice Munro (Nobel Prize in Literature 2013), Michael Ondaatje (The English Patient), Yann Martel (Life of Pi), Lucy Maud Montgomery (Anne of Green Gables).
cinema: Denis Villeneuve (Dune, Arrival, Blade Runner 2049), James Cameron (Titanic, Avatar), David Cronenberg, Sarah Polley; TIFF is world's premier Oscar launchpad.
sports: Ice Hockey (national winter sport; 9-time Olympic Gold medalists; NHL), Lacrosse (national summer sport), Basketball (invented by Canadian James Naismith; Toronto Raptors NBA champions), Curling, Canadian Football (CFL).
media: CBC/Radio-Canada, The Globe and Mail, Toronto Star, National Post, CTV, Global News.
clothing: Canada Goose parkas, Hudson's Bay point blankets, plaid flannel lumberjack shirts, Cowichan hand-knitted wool sweaters.
holidays: National Day for Truth and Reconciliation (September 30)
crafts: Inuit soapstone and whalebone carvings, West Coast First Nations totem poles and cedar bentwood boxes, hand-quilted Quebec textiles.
worldHeritageSites: Canadian Rocky Mountain Parks (Banff, Jasper, Yoho, Kootenay)
Historic District of Old Québec
Nahanni National Park Reserve
Gros Morne National Park
L'Anse aux Meadows National Historic Site
Dinosaur Provincial Park
unescoIntangible: Indigenous ceremonial knowledge and maple syrup harvesting traditions
flagDescription: Red field with a white square in the center (1:2:1 ratio, Canadian pale) bearing a stylized, 11-pointed red maple leaf.
coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by the English lion holding the Union flag and the Scottish unicorn holding the royal banner of France, flanking a shield depicting lions of England, lion of Scotland, harp of Ireland, and fleurs-de-lis of France, under three red maple leaves, surmounted by St. Edward's Crown, with motto 'A MARI USQUE AD MARE'.
travelNotes: Extremely safe, welcoming, and visually grand; world-class national parks system; bilingual signs across federal facilities.
shortSummary: Canada is the world's second-largest country by area, spanning six time zones from the Atlantic to the Pacific and Arctic oceans, famed for the majestic Canadian Rockies, pristine boreal wilderness, vibrant multicultural cities, and ice hockey passion.

name: Costa Rica
motto: ¡Vivan siempre el trabajo y la paz! (Long live work and peace!)
longestRiver: San Juan River border / Reventazón River
climate: Tropical and subtropical; dry season December to April; green season May to November
biodiversity: Holds 5% of world's total biodiversity on 0.03% of Earth's landmass; over 28% of territory protected in national parks
latestElections: General election 2022; municipal 2024; general election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Model of democratic stability, environmental governance, clean energy, and high-tech semiconductor investment.
foreignRelations: Member of OECD, UN, OAS, SICA; host of UN University for Peace; global champion of environmental peace and disarmament.
military: Abolished in 1949; civilian Public Force (Fuerza Pública) and Coast Guard.
history: Inhabited by Diquís, Huetar, and Chorotega peoples. Christopher Columbus landed in 1502, naming it 'Costa Rica' (Rich Coast). Gained independence from Spain in 1821 and formed part of the Federal Republic of Central America. Following the brief 1948 civil war, visionary leader José Figueres Ferrer abolished the military in the 1949 Constitution, dedicating national budgets to health and education.
recentEvents2020_2026: Joined the OECD as a full member; generated over 99% of electricity from renewable sources for nine consecutive years; expanded medical device and semiconductor export hubs.
historicalFigures: Óscar Arias Sánchez (Nobel Peace Prize laureate 1987)
Franklin Chang Díaz (Astronaut and plasma physicist)
lifeExpectancy: 80.8 years (highest in Central America; home to Nicoya Blue Zone)
education: University of Costa Rica (UCR) and Tecnológico de Costa Rica (TEC); free universal public schooling.
healthcare: Caja Costarricense de Seguro Social (CCSS / La Caja) provides universal public healthcare coverage.
socialCustoms: 'Pura Vida' (Pure Life) philosophy greeting, friendly relaxed lifestyle, family Sunday meals.
etiquette: Gentle, non-confrontational, polite greetings ('Buenos días'), punctuality respected in business.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated for peace without an army, extraordinary rainforest biodiversity, ecotourism excellence, and the joyful 'Pura Vida' philosophy.
industries: Medical devices and precision equipment (#1 export)
naturalResources: Exceptional hydropower, geothermal, and wind energy
energy: 99%+ renewable electricity: Hydroelectric (73%), Geothermal (14%), Wind (12%), Solar and biomass (1%)
tourism: Over 3.5 million international travelers visiting Monteverde Cloud Forest, Arenal Volcano, Manuel Antonio National Park, and Tortuguero.
employment: Unemployment approx. 7.8%; high technical and medical technology manufacturing employment.
debtInflation: Inflation normalized around central bank 3% target; investment-grade fiscal consolidation.
transport: Pan-American Highway (Ruta 2 and Ruta 1); San José urban passenger rail.
airports: Juan Santamaría International Airport (SJO in Alajuela/San José)
Daniel Oduber Quirós International (LIR in Liberia)
cuisine: Gallo Pinto (rice and black beans with Lizano sauce), Casado (traditional plate with rice, beans, plantains, salad, and meat), Olla de carne, Ceviche tico, Tres leches cake, Gourmet Tarrazú coffee.
festivals: Fiestas de Zapote (San José - bull running and parades)
Limon Carnival (Afro-Caribbean heritage in October)
Independence Day (Torch of Freedom run)
music: Cumbia costarricense, Calypso limonense (Walter Ferguson), Marimba music, Rock en español.
dance: Punto Guanacasteco (national folk dance), Salsa, Merengue.
art: Pre-Columbian Diquís stone spheres, brightly painted Sarchí oxcarts, contemporary landscape canvases.
architecture: Teatro Nacional de Costa Rica (neoclassical gem in San José), eco-lodges designed in harmony with tropical nature.
literature: Carmen Lyra (Cuentos de mi Tía Panchita), Joaquín Gutiérrez, Carlos Luis Fallas (Mamita Yunai).
cinema: Hernán Jiménez (A ojos cerrados, Then Came You); acclaimed environmental documentary productions.
sports: Football (national team 'Los Ticos' - 2014 World Cup quarter-finalists; Keylor Navas 3-time Champions League winner), Surfing (world-class Pacific breaks), Whitewater rafting.
media: La Nación, La República, Teletica (Canal 7), Repretel, Amelia Rueda.
clothing: Traditional Guanacasteco white dresses with ruffled multi-colored trim; modern western attire in San José.
crafts: Hand-painted traditional wooden oxcarts (Carretas de Sarchí - UNESCO Intangible Heritage), Boruca indigenous carved balsa masks.
worldHeritageSites: Precolumbian Chiefdom Settlements with Stone Spheres of the Diquís
Area de Conservación Guanacaste
Cocos Island National Park
Talamanca Range-La Amistad Reserves
unescoIntangible: Oxherding and oxcart traditions in Costa Rica (inscribed 2008)
famousPeople: Christiana Figueres (architect of Paris Climate Agreement)
flagDescription: Five horizontal bands of blue (top and bottom), white, red (double width, center), white, and blue, inspired by the French Tricolore.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features three smoking volcanoes between two oceans with merchant ships, a rising sun, seven stars for the seven provinces, and banner 'AMERICA CENTRAL / REPUBLICA DE COSTA RICA'.
travelNotes: Pristine ecotourism capital of the Americas; peaceful, safe, highly welcoming with 'Pura Vida' ethos.
shortSummary: Costa Rica is a peaceful global pioneer of ecological conservation and renewable energy, celebrated for abolishing its military in 1949, protecting 28% of its territory in lush national parks, and welcoming travelers with the warm spirit of 'Pura Vida'.
sources: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Censos (INEC Costa Rica)

name: Cuba
nationalDay: January 1 (Triumph of the Revolution) / October 10 (Independence Day)
motto: Patria o Muerte, Venceremos (Fatherland or Death, We Shall Overcome)
climate: Tropical moderated by trade winds; dry season November to April; rainy season May to October
biodiversity: Largest and most biodiverse island in the Caribbean, home to the bee hummingbird (world's smallest bird) and Montecristo Cuban solenodon
latestElections: Parliamentary election 2023; municipal 2022
politicalSituation: Economic restructuring, micro-enterprise (Mipymes) regulation, energy grid revitalization, and foreign joint-venture development.
foreignRelations: Founding member of ALBA, UN, CELAC, Non-Aligned Movement; strategic ties with China, Russia, and Latin American partners.
military: Revolutionary Armed Forces (FAR: Revolutionary Army, Revolutionary Navy, Air and Air Defense Force) and Youth Labor Army.
adminDivisions: 15 provinces and 1 special municipality (Isla de la Juventud)
history: Inhabited by Taíno and Guanahatabey peoples. Christopher Columbus arrived in 1492. Spanish colonial rule established Havana as the treasure fleet hub of the Americas. The Ten Years' War (1868–1878) and 1895 War of Independence led by José Martí preceded US intervention in the Spanish-American War (1898). Independence achieved in 1902. Fidel Castro led the 26th of July Movement, overthrowing the Batista dictatorship in 1959 and aligning with the Soviet Union, leading to the 1962 Cuban Missile Crisis. Survived the post-Soviet 'Special Period' to develop world-renowned healthcare and biotechnology sectors.
recentEvents2020_2026: Approved progressive new Family Code legalizing marriage equality in referendum; developed domestic sovereign COVID vaccines (Abdala, Soberana); implemented macroeconomic currency unification reforms.
literacyRate: 99.8% (one of the highest in the world)
education: University of Havana (founded 1728) and Latin American School of Medicine (ELAM); free universal education from primary through postgraduate levels.
healthcare: Universal publicly funded healthcare system renowned for doctor-to-patient ratio (over 8 doctors per 1,000 citizens) and international medical brigades.
socialCustoms: Vibrant street music, domino games played on sidewalks, sharing strong Cuban espresso (cafecito), classic vintage car culture.
etiquette: Warm, expressive, passionate conversationalists, animated gestures, polite handshakes and cheek kisses.
nationalIdentity: Defined by fierce national sovereignty, rich Afro-Cuban musical rhythm, vintage classic cars, cigars, and boxing/baseball excellence.
agriculture: Tobacco (Vuelta Abajo - world's finest cigar leaf)
energy: Crude oil and gas thermal (80%), Solar, wind, and sugarcane biomass (15%), floating power plants
tourism: Over 3.2 million international travelers visiting Old Havana, Varadero beaches, Viñales Valley mogotes, and Trinidad.
employment: State sector, cooperative farms, and burgeoning private micro-enterprises (Mipymes).
debtInflation: Macroeconomic restructuring, managing foreign exchange liquidity and debt repayment under bilateral agreements.
transport: Autopista Nacional; historic Hershey Electric Railway; vintage 1950s American cars (almendrones) operating as collective taxis.
airports: José Martí International Airport (HAV in Havana)
Juan Gualberto Gómez International (VRA in Varadero)
ports: Port of Mariel (state-of-the-art deepwater container mega-terminal and Special Development Zone)
cuisine: Ropa Vieja (shredded flank steak in tomato sauce), Moros y Cristianos (black beans and white rice), Lechón asado (roast suckling pig with mojo criollo garlic-citrus sauce), Tostones, Yuca con mojo, Mojito, Daiquiri, Cuba Libre.
festivals: Festival Internacional del Nuevo Cine Latinoamericano (Havana)
Carnaval de Santiago de Cuba
Havana Jazz Festival
Festival del Habano
music: Son cubano, Rumba, Danzón, Mambo, Cha-cha-chá, Salsa / Timba, Trova, Nueva Trova (Silvio Rodríguez, Pablo Milanés), Buena Vista Social Club.
dance: Salsa cubana (Casino), Rumba (Yambú, Guaguancó, Columbia - UNESCO), Danzón, Ballet Nacional de Cuba (Alicia Alonso).
art: Wifredo Lam (surrealist master), René Portocarrero, Amelia Peláez, Fusterlandia mosaic art in Jaimanitas.
architecture: Old Havana Spanish colonial baroque, Art Nouveau and Art Deco in Vedado, neoclassical mansions, Malecón seawall promenade.
literature: José Martí, Alejo Carpentier (pioneer of 'the marvelous real'), Nicolás Guillén (National Poet), Dulce María Loynaz (Cervantes Prize).
cinema: ICAIC (Cuban Film Institute), Memories of Underdevelopment (Tomás Gutiérrez Alea), Strawberry and Chocolate (Oscar nominated).
sports: Baseball (the national passion; 3-time Olympic Champions), Boxing (legendary Olympic powerhouse: Teófilo Stevenson, Félix Savón), Athletics, Wrestling.
media: Granma, Juventud Rebelde, Cubadebate, Tele Rebelde, Cubavisión.
clothing: Guayabera (traditional four-pocket embroidered dress shirt, declared official formal national garment), casual tropical clothing.
holidays: July 26 (Day of National Rebellion / Moncada Barracks)
crafts: Hand-rolled cigars, humidors made of cedarwood, leatherwork, ceramic pottery.
worldHeritageSites: Old Havana and its Fortification System
Trinidad and the Valley de los Ingenios
Viñales Valley
San Pedro de la Roca Castle (Santiago)
Desembarco del Granma National Park
unescoIntangible: Rumba in Cuba: a festive combination of music and dances
Cuban Bolero
Tumba Francesa musical tradition
flagDescription: Five alternating horizontal stripes of blue (three) and white (two), with a red equilateral triangle based on the hoist containing a white five-pointed star.
coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by oak and laurel branches, featuring an oval shield displaying a golden key between two capes (symbolizing Cuba as the Key to the Gulf of Mexico), blue and white diagonal stripes, and a royal palm on green hills, topped by a red Phrygian cap of liberty with a star.

symbols.bird: Cuban trogon (Tocororo - plumage matches the flag colors)

landmarks: Old Havana & Plaza de la Catedral
travelNotes: Captivating cultural and historical destination; vibrant music and art scene; warm and hospitable people.
shortSummary: Cuba is the largest island in the Caribbean, celebrated for the colonial grandeur of Old Havana, its revolutionary history, vintage classic cars, world-record boxing heroes, and infectious musical rhythms from Son to Salsa.
sources: Oficina Nacional de Estadística e Información (ONEI Cuba)

name: Dominica
nationalAnthem: Isle of Beauty, Isle of Splendour
motto: Après Bondie, C'est La Ter (After God, the Earth)
majorLakes: Boiling Lake (world's second largest boiling lake)
climate: Tropical rainy with lush cloud forests
biodiversity: The Nature Island of the Caribbean; over 60% forested with 365 rivers, waterfalls, and the world's first sperm whale sanctuary
headOfState: President Sylvanie Burton (first Indigenous Kalinago president)
latestElections: General election 2022; presidential election 2023
politicalSituation: National climate resilience strategy aiming to become the world's first climate-resilient nation; development of geothermal energy and international airport.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; designated world's first marine protected area for sperm whales in 2023.
military: No standing army; Commonwealth of Dominica Police Force and Coast Guard.
history: Home to the Kalinago (Carib) people who resisted colonization longer than any other Caribbean community; Kalinago Territory preserved in eastern Dominica. Christopher Columbus sailed past on a Sunday in 1493 (naming it Dominica). Ceded to Britain in 1763. Gained independence in 1978 under Patrick John. Dame Eugenia Charles became the Caribbean's first female prime minister in 1980.
recentEvents2020_2026: Elected Sylvanie Burton as the first female and first Indigenous Kalinago head of state in 2023; broke ground on the multi-million-dollar international airport; commissioned national geothermal power plant.
historicalFigures: Dame Eugenia Charles (Iron Lady of the Caribbean)
education: Dominica State College; universal primary and secondary education.
healthcare: Dominica China Friendship Hospital in Roseau and modern district wellness centres.
socialCustoms: Creole Day (Jounen Kwéyòl) celebrations, Bouyon music street dancing, Kalinago basket-weaving traditions.
etiquette: Warm, respectful, greeting everyone upon entering buses or shops, community solidarity.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as 'The Nature Island', guardian of Kalinago indigenous heritage, boiling volcanic lakes, and pristine waterfalls.
sectors: Services & Tourism 65%, Agriculture 18%, Construction & Energy 12%, Industry 5%
energy: Advancing to 100% renewable electricity via geothermal power (Roseau Valley), hydro, and solar
tourism: Premier ecotourism haven: hiking the 185-km Waitukubuli National Trail (first long-distance trail in the Caribbean), Boiling Lake, Trafalgar Falls, and year-round sperm whale watching.
employment: Agriculture and fisheries, public administration, eco-lodges and dive guiding.
debtInflation: XCD pegged to USD at 2.70:1; investments driven by Citizenship by Investment revenue.
transport: Paved coastal roads; inter-island ferries to Martinique, Guadeloupe, and St. Lucia.
airports: New Dominica International Airport under construction
cuisine: Callaloo soup (national dish made from dasheen leaves, meat, and coconut milk), Mountain chicken (historic frog delicacy), Fish broth, Roast breadfruit, Plantain, Soursop juice.
festivals: World Creole Music Festival (WCMF in October)
Independence and Heritage Day Celebrations
Mas Domnik (The Real Mas Carnival)
music: Bouyon music (indigenous genre created by WCK), Cadence-lypso (Exile One), Jing ping, Reggae.
dance: Quadrille, Bele dance, Bouyon jumping.
art: Kalinago woven larouma reed baskets, carved calabash gourds, vibrant landscape paintings.
architecture: Morne Trois Pitons wooden eco-lodges, colonial timber architecture in Roseau with gingerbread fretwork.
literature: Jean Rhys (Wide Sargasso Sea - world-famous novel set in colonial Dominica), Phyllis Shand Allfrey (The Orchid House).
cinema: Filming location for Pirates of the Caribbean: Dead Man's Chest and At World's End (filmed along Indian River and Morne Trois Pitons).
sports: Cricket (Windsor Park Stadium), Athletics (Thea LaFond - historic first-ever Olympic Gold medal for Dominica in triple jump at Paris 2024).
media: The Chronicle, Dominica News Online, DBS Radio, Kairi FM.
clothing: National costume: Wob Dwiyet (elaborate Creole dress with bright madras fabric and foulard scarf).
crafts: Kalinago handwoven reed baskets (larouma grass), carved wood canoes, pottery.
worldHeritageSites: Morne Trois Pitons National Park (including Boiling Lake, Valley of Desolation, and Emerald Pool)
unescoIntangible: Kalinago craft traditions and Dominican Bouyon musical heritage
famousPeople: Thea LaFond (Olympic Gold medalist triple jumper 2024)
flagDescription: Green field with a centered cross of three bands (yellow, black, white), bearing a red central disc with the Sisserou parrot encircled by ten lime-green five-pointed stars.
coatOfArmsDescription: Quartered shield showing a coconut tree, a crapeau frog, a sailing canoe, and a banana tree, supported by two Sisserou parrots, with motto 'APRÈS BONDIE, C'EST LA TER'.
travelNotes: The Nature Island of the Caribbean; lush hiking, diving, and ethical whale watching paradise.
shortSummary: Dominica is the breathtaking 'Nature Island' of the Caribbean, covered in emerald rainforests and 365 rivers, home to the second-largest boiling lake in the world, the Kalinago indigenous territory, and the first national marine sanctuary for sperm whales.

name: Dominican Republic
nationalAnthem: Himno Nacional de la República Dominicana
motto: Dios, Patria, Libertad (God, Fatherland, Liberty)
highestPoint: Pico Duarte (3,098 m - highest peak in the Caribbean)
lowestPoint: Lake Enriquillo (-46 m - lowest point in the Caribbean)
majorLakes: Lake Enriquillo (hypersaline lake with American crocodiles)
climate: Tropical maritime with moderate temperature variation
environmentalIssues: Soil erosion and coral reef protection
biodiversity: Home to Caribbean high peaks, Jaragua National Park, humpback whale nursery in Samaná Bay, and endemic Hispaniolan solenodon
legislature: Congress of the Republic (Senate and Chamber of Deputies)
latestElections: General election May 2024 (Luis Abinader re-elected in first round)
politicalSituation: Strong macroeconomic growth (fastest-growing economy in Latin America over recent decades); port modernization; anti-corruption initiatives.
foreignRelations: Member of CAFTA-DR, UN, OAS, SICA, CELAC; strong economic partnership with the United States.
military: Military Forces of the Dominican Republic (Army, Navy, Air Force) and National Police.
history: Inhabited by the Taíno people (who called the island Quisqueya). Columbus established La Isabela in 1493; Santo Domingo founded in 1496 became the first permanent European settlement and university in the Americas. Gained independence from Spain in 1821, was occupied by Haiti, and fought the Dominican War of Independence under Juan Pablo Duarte in 1844. Survived the Trujillo dictatorship (1930–1961) to emerge as one of Latin America's strongest democratic and economic performers.
recentEvents2020_2026: President Luis Abinader re-elected in May 2024; surpassed 10 million annual tourist arrivals; completed Santo Domingo Metro expansion and Monorail in Santiago.
education: Universidad Autónoma de Santo Domingo (UASD - founded 1538, oldest university in the Americas) and INTEC.
healthcare: National Health Insurance (SeNaSa) achieves near-universal population health insurance enrollment.
socialCustoms: Playing dominoes in open-air colmados, dancing Bachata and Merengue in public plazas, passionate baseball discussions.
etiquette: Warm handshakes, polite formal greetings ('Buenos días'), family-oriented hospitality.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the cradle of colonial Americas history, Merengue and Bachata rhythms, and immense Major League Baseball pride.
sectors: Services & Tourism 60%, Industry & Free Zones 28%, Agriculture 6%, Mining 6%
industries: Free trade zone manufacturing (medical devices, electronics)
Tourism and luxury resort hospitality (Punta Cana)
Gold and ferronickel mining (Pueblo Viejo gold mine - one of world's largest)
naturalResources: Amber and Larimar (blue gemstone unique to Dominican Republic)
energy: Natural gas (39%), Coal (30%), Solar and wind (17%), Hydro (10%), Fuel oil (4%)
tourism: Over 10.5 million international travelers visiting Punta Cana, Cap Cana, Puerto Plata, Samaná Peninsula, and the Colonial City of Santo Domingo.
employment: Unemployment approx. 5.1%; robust formal job creation in free zones, tourism, and construction.
debtInflation: Inflation anchored within Central Bank target (4% ± 1%); investment-grade path supported by sovereign stability.
transport: Santo Domingo Metro and Cable Car (Teleférico); Santiago Monorail; modern Autovía del Este highway network.
airports: Punta Cana International (PUJ - busiest airport in the Caribbean)
Las Américas International (SDQ in Santo Domingo)
cuisine: La Bandera Dominicana (national lunch: white rice, red beans, stewed meat, and fried sweet plantains), Mangú (mashed green plantains with salami, fried cheese, and eggs / Los Tres Golpes), Sancocho (seven-meat hearty stew), Mofongo, Chicharrón, Mamajuana herbal spiced rum.
festivals: Carnaval Dominicano (featuring Diablo Cojuelo masks in La Vega and Santo Domingo)
Festival del Merengue
Presidente Festival of Latin Music
music: Merengue (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Bachata (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Dembow dominicano, Latin trap.
dance: Merengue, Bachata (danced worldwide, created in Dominican barrios), Son dominicano.
art: Cándido Bidó, Guillo Pérez, colorful Taíno-inspired naive paintings, amber and larimar jewelry.
architecture: Ciudad Colonial de Santo Domingo (first cathedral, first hospital, first paved street in the Americas); modern Caribbean resort architecture.
literature: Juan Bosch, Julia Alvarez (In the Time of the Butterflies), Junot Díaz (The Brief Wondrous Life of Oscar Wao - Pulitzer Prize winner).
cinema: Vibrant local film industry supported by national film law (DGCINE) and Pinewood Dominican Republic Studios.
sports: Baseball (the national religion; Dominican Republic produces more MLB superstars than any foreign nation: Pedro Martínez, David Ortiz, Albert Pujols, Vladimir Guerrero, Juan Soto), Basketball, Volleyball (Las Reinas del Caribe).
media: Listín Diario, Diario Libre, El Caribe, CDN, Color Visión, Telemicro.
clothing: Guayabera shirts and linen clothing; colorful Diablo Cojuelo satin carnival costumes.
crafts: Larimar and amber jewelry, faceless Limé ceramic dolls (Muñecas Limé), hand-rolled cigars, carved mahogany rocking chairs.
worldHeritageSites: Colonial City of Santo Domingo (first European settlement in the Americas, designated 1990)
unescoIntangible: Music and dance of the Dominican Merengue
Music and dance of Dominican Bachata
Cultural space of the Brotherhood of the Holy Spirit of the Congos of Villa Mella
flagDescription: A centered white cross extends to the edges and divides the flag into four rectangles: blue (top hoist and bottom fly) and red (bottom hoist and top fly), with the national coat of arms centered on the cross.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a shield showing an open Bible opened to John 8:32 ('Y la verdad os hará libres') beneath a golden cross and six spears, flanked by laurel and palm branches, topped by the blue motto banner 'DIOS, PATRIA, LIBERTAD'.
landmarks: Colonial City of Santo Domingo & Cathedral of Santa María la Menor
travelNotes: The Caribbean's #1 tourist destination; outstanding highway connectivity, luxury all-inclusive resorts, and historic colonial charm.
shortSummary: The Dominican Republic is the Caribbean's economic and tourism powerhouse, celebrated as the historic cradle of European settlement in the Americas, the homeland of Merengue and Bachata, and a legendary exporter of baseball icons and fine cigars.

name: El Salvador
motto: Dios, Unión, Libertad (God, Union, Liberty)
climate: Tropical with distinct wet season (May to October) and dry season (November to April); temperate in mountain highlands
environmentalIssues: Soil erosion and river basin rehabilitation
biodiversity: Volcanic national parks (Cerro Verde, El Imposible), mangrove estuaries of Jiquilisco Bay, and Pacific sea turtle nesting beaches
currency: United States Dollar (USD, $) / Bitcoin (BTC - legal tender)
latestElections: General election February 2024 (Nayib Bukele re-elected in landslide)
politicalSituation: Dramatic transformation of domestic security through Territorial Control Plan, reduction of homicide rates to lowest in Latin America; pioneer in Bitcoin adoption.
foreignRelations: Member of SICA, UN, OAS, CELAC; strong economic links with the US diaspora and expanding Asian trade partnerships.
military: Armed Forces of El Salvador (Army, Navy, Air Force) and National Civil Police (PNC).
history: Inhabited by the Pipil people (who called it Cuzcatlán / Place of Precious Jewels) and Lenca. Spanish conquest led by Pedro de Alvarado in 1524. Independence declared in 1821 from Spain. The 20th century saw the 1932 indigenous uprising (La Matanza) and the brutal 1980–1992 Civil War that ended with the UN-brokered Chapultepec Peace Accords. Adopted the US dollar in 2001. In 2019, Nayib Bukele was elected president, transforming national security and declaring Bitcoin legal tender in 2021.
recentEvents2020_2026: Nayib Bukele won re-election in February 2024 with over 84% of votes; inaugurated National Library of El Salvador (BINAES); hosted Miss Universe 2023; expanded 'Surf City' coastal infrastructure.
historicalFigures: Saint Óscar Romero (Archbishop and martyr, canonized 2018)
education: University of El Salvador (UES) and Universidad Centroamericana José Simeón Cañas (UCA); 'Enlaces con la Educación' student laptop distribution.
healthcare: National integrated public hospital network (including Hospital El Salvador) administered by the Ministry of Health and ISSS.
socialCustoms: Eating pupusas at local pupuserías, Sunday family visits to Lake Coatepeque, vibrant surf culture on the Pacific coast.
etiquette: Warm handshakes, polite address using 'Don' and 'Doña', hospitable and resilient demeanor.
nationalIdentity: Defined by pride in pupusas, volcanic dramatic landscapes, world-class surf breaks, and historic security renaissance.
industries: Information technology and business process outsourcing
energy: Over 75% clean energy: Geothermal (25%), Hydroelectric (30%), Solar and biomass (20%), Fuel thermal (25%)
tourism: Over 3.4 million international visitors flocking to 'Surf City' (El Tunco, El Zonte / Bitcoin Beach), Santa Ana Volcano hikes, Ruta de las Flores, and Joya de Cerén.
employment: Formal employment expanding in tourism, tech services, and construction; substantial diaspora remittances support.
debtInflation: Inflation low and controlled due to dollarization; public debt reprofiled under fiscal stabilization.
transport: Carretera Panamericana (Pan-American Highway); coastal highway (Litoral) connecting surf hubs; modern Pacific railway projects.
airports: El Salvador International Airport Saint Óscar Arnulfo Romero y Galdámez (SAL in San Luis Talpa - major Avianca hub)
ports: Port of Acajutla (primary commercial freight gateway)
cuisine: Pupusas (thick handmade corn tortillas stuffed with cheese, chicharrón, and refried beans, served with curtido pickled cabbage and tomato salsa), Tamales pisques, Sopa de pata, Yuca frita con chicharrón, Empanadas de plátano, Horchata de morro.
festivals: Fiestas Agostinas (August patron saint festivals honoring El Salvador del Mundo)
National Pupusa Day (second Sunday in November)
Bolas de Fuego festival in Nejapa (September 15 fireballs)
music: Cumbia salvadoreña (Marito Rivera, Hermanos Flores), Marimba, Folkloric Pipil tunes, Rock en español.
dance: El Carbonero, Danza de los Historiantes, Torito Pinto.
art: Fernando Llort (creator of iconic colorful La Palma naive folk art style), pre-Columbian Pipil polychrome pottery.
architecture: Joya de Cerén (UNESCO World Heritage Site: the 'Pompeii of the Americas', buried under Laguna Caldera ash ~600 CE); San Salvador Cathedral (crypt of Saint Óscar Romero); ultra-modern BINAES National Library.
literature: Roque Dalton (legendary revolutionary poet: Poemas clandestinos), Salarrué (Cuentos de barro), Claudia Lars, Manlio Argueta.
cinema: Documentaries on historical memory and modern transformation; thriving indie short-film community.
sports: Football (Mágico González - legendary global football genius admired by Maradona; Estadio Cuscatlán), Surfing (ISA World Surfing Games host), Beach Soccer (world-ranked national team).
media: La Prensa Gráfica, El Diario de Hoy, Canal 12, Canal 4, Canal 21, El Faro (digital).
clothing: Traditional white cotton traje de campesino with blue sash; modern western casual wear.
crafts: La Palma colorful painted woodcrafts, Ilobasco clay miniatures, San Sebastián woven cotton textiles.
worldHeritageSites: Joya de Cerén Archaeological Site (extraordinarily preserved pre-Columbian village buried by volcanic ash)
unescoIntangible: Traditional craftsmanship of pupusas and La Palma folk art
flagDescription: Horizontal triband of cobalt blue, white, and cobalt blue, with the national coat of arms centered on the white band.
coatOfArmsDescription: Equilateral triangle containing five volcanoes rising between two oceans, a red Phrygian cap of liberty on a staff radiating golden light, and rainbow, surrounded by the golden inscription 'REPÚBLICA DE EL SALVADOR EN LA AMÉRICA CENTRAL' and fourteen laurel clusters.
landmarks: San Salvador Historic Downtown & BINAES Library
travelNotes: Remarkable safety turnaround; world's premier year-round surfing waves; friendly people and famous pupusas.
shortSummary: El Salvador is the vibrant 'Land of Volcanoes' on the Pacific rim, renowned for its dramatic security transformation, world-class surf breaks along 'Surf City', the preserved ancient village of Joya de Cerén, and delicious pupusas.
sources: Banco Central de Reserva de El Salvador

name: Grenada
motto: Ever Conscious of God We Aspire, Build and Advance as One People
climate: Tropical rainy with trade winds; dry season January to May; wet season June to December
naturalHazards: Kick 'em Jenny active submarine volcano off north coast
biodiversity: The 'Isle of Spice'; lush rainforests, Annandale Falls, nesting leatherback sea turtles at Levera Beach
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Dame Cécile La Grenade)
latestElections: General election 2022; general election scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell guiding sustainable economic transformation, climate diplomacy, and expansion of digital education.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; champion of small island green and blue economies.
military: No standing army; Royal Grenada Police Force (RGPF) and Coast Guard.
adminDivisions: 6 parishes and 1 dependency (Carriacou and Petite Martinique)
history: Inhabited by indigenous Caribs (Kalinago). Sighted by Columbus in 1498 (named Concepción). French founded Fort Royal (St. George's) in 1650. Ceded to Britain in 1763; Julien Fédon led major 1795 rebellion against British rule. Gained independence on February 7, 1974 under Sir Eric Gairy. The 1979 New Jewel Movement led by Maurice Bishop established the People's Revolutionary Government until internal crisis led to the 1983 US military intervention (Operation Urgent Fury) and restoration of constitutional democracy.
recentEvents2020_2026: Celebrated 50th Golden Jubilee of Independence in February 2024; PM Dickon Mitchell assumed chairmanship of CARICOM; expanded marine conservation and organic spice exports.
education: St. George's University (SGU - world-renowned medical and veterinary school educating thousands of global physicians) and T.A. Marryshow Community College.
healthcare: General Hospital in St. George's, Princess Alice Hospital in Mirabeau, and Princess Royal Hospital in Carriacou.
socialCustoms: Spicemas Carnival (Jab Jab masquerade), sharing Oil Down communal feasts, cricket gatherings, storytelling.
etiquette: Friendly and respectful, polite 'Good morning' greetings, community hospitality.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated as the 'Isle of Spice' (produces 20% of world nutmeg), home to the world's first underwater sculpture park, and Olympic track greatness.
industries: Artisan single-origin organic chocolate (Grenada Chocolate Company)
agriculture: Nutmeg and mace (world's top producer per capita)
energy: Expanding solar installations and geothermal exploration on Mount Saint Catherine
exports: Fine organic chocolate and cocoa beans
tourism: Over 550,000 visitors enjoying Grand Anse Beach (consistently ranked among world's top 10 beaches), Molinere Underwater Sculpture Park, Grand Etang crater lake, and spice plantation tours.
employment: Medical university operations, tourism hospitality, spice agriculture.
debtInflation: XCD pegged 2.70:1 to USD; low and stable inflation.
transport: Paved scenic coastal roads; Osprey ferry connecting Grenada to Carriacou.
airports: Maurice Bishop International Airport (GND at Point Salines)
ports: Port of St. George's (horseshoe-shaped deepwater harbor / Carenage)
cuisine: Oil Down (national one-pot dish: salted meat, chicken, breadfruit, callaloo, and dumplings stewed in rich coconut milk and turmeric until absorbed), Nutmeg ice cream, Fresh grilled fish, Roti, Cocoa tea, Clarke's Court and River Antoine rum.
festivals: Spicemas (August Carnival famous for Jab Jab devil masquerade with black molasses and horns)
Carriacou Maroon and String Band Music Festival
Grenada Chocolate Festival
music: Soca, Calypso, Traditional stringband music of Carriacou, Reggae.
dance: Jab Jab carnival dance, Big Drum Dance of Carriacou (ancient West African ancestral dance preserved for centuries).
art: Molinere Underwater Sculpture Park (created by Jason deCaires Taylor - world's first underwater sculpture garden), vibrant Caribbean canvases.
architecture: Georgian brick and stone colonial buildings with fish-scale tiles in St. George's (often called the prettiest harbor town in the Caribbean); Fort George.
literature: Merle Collins (Angel, The Colour of Forgetting), Jacob Ross (The Bone Readers).
cinema: Documentaries on the Grenadian Revolution and world-class marine conservation.
sports: Athletics (Kirani James - Olympic Gold 2012, Silver 2016, Bronze 2021 in 400m; Lindon Victor - Olympic Bronze 2024 decathlon), Cricket (National Cricket Stadium).
media: The Grenadian Voice, The New Today, GBN (Grenada Broadcasting Network).
clothing: National costume in vibrant yellow, red, and green madras; casual island wear.
crafts: Nutmeg and spice baskets, woven straw hats, calabash carvings, sea-glass jewelry.
worldHeritageSites: Tentative List: Historic District of St. George's, Grenadines Island Group
unescoIntangible: Big Drum Dance of Carriacou and Spicemas Jab Jab traditions
flagDescription: Rectangular flag with a red border containing six yellow five-pointed stars (top and bottom); central rectangle divided into four triangles (two yellow, two green) bearing a red central disc with a large yellow star, and a stylized nutmeg clove in the hoist triangle.
coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by an armadillo and a Ramier pigeon, showing Columbus's ship Santa María, topped by seven roses and a golden helmet, with motto 'EVER CONSCIOUS OF GOD WE ASPIRE, BUILD AND ADVANCE AS ONE PEOPLE'.
landmarks: Grand Etang National Park & Crater Lake
River Antoine Rum Distillery (powered by water wheel since 1785)
travelNotes: The Isle of Spice; enchanting, safe, aromatic tropical paradise with world-famous diving and beaches.
shortSummary: Grenada is the captivating 'Isle of Spice' in the southern Caribbean, renowned for producing fragrant nutmeg and fine chocolate, the world's first underwater sculpture park, the pristine sands of Grand Anse, and Olympic track champions.

name: Guatemala
motto: El País de la Eterna Primavera (The Country of Eternal Spring)
highestPoint: Volcán Tajumulco (4,220 m - highest point in Central America)
climate: Tropical in coastal lowlands; temperate highland climate ('Eternal Spring') in central plateau
environmentalIssues: Deforestation in the Maya Biosphere Reserve
Watershed pollution in Lake Amatitlán and Lake Atitlán
biodiversity: Megadiverse hotspot hosting the Maya Biosphere Reserve (second largest rainforest block in the Americas after the Amazon), resplendent quetzals, and jaguars
latestElections: General election 2023 (Bernardo Arévalo inaugurated January 2024)
politicalSituation: Administration of anti-corruption reformist President Bernardo Arévalo; focus on strengthening institutional rule of law, indigenous community rights, and infrastructure.
foreignRelations: Member of SICA, UN, OAS, CELAC, WTO; maintains diplomatic relations with Taiwan; strong ties with the US.
military: Armed Forces of Guatemala (Army, Navy, Air Force) and National Civil Police (PNC).
history: Heart of the classical Maya civilization: monumental city-states of Tikal, El Mirador, Quiriguá, and Yaxha. Conquered by Pedro de Alvarado in 1524, establishing the Captaincy General of Guatemala. Declared independence from Spain in 1821. Suffered a 36-year internal armed conflict (1960–1996) that ended with the landmark 1996 Peace Accords recognizing indigenous rights. Democratic consolidation deepened with the historic anti-corruption election of Bernardo Arévalo in 2023.
recentEvents2020_2026: Inaugurated President Bernardo Arévalo in January 2024 following peaceful popular defense of democracy; celebrated 20th anniversary of UNESCO recognition of Tikal and Semana Santa.
historicalFigures: Miguel Ángel Asturias (Nobel Prize in Literature 1967)
Rigoberta Menchú Tum (Nobel Peace Prize laureate 1992)
education: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala (USAC - founded 1676, third oldest in the Americas) and Universidad del Valle; intercultural bilingual education.
healthcare: Hospital San Juan de Dios and Hospital Roosevelt in Guatemala City alongside IGSS social security hospitals.
socialCustoms: Semana Santa (Holy Week) elaborate sawdust carpets (alfombras) in Antigua, wearing traditional backstrap-loom woven huipiles, market day barter.
etiquette: Polite greetings, respectful address to elders, modest and courteous conversation.
nationalIdentity: Defined by unbroken ancient Maya civilizational heritage, colorful woven textiles, majestic volcanoes, and Lake Atitlán.
energy: Over 70% renewable: Hydroelectric (45%), Sugarcane biomass (15%), Geothermal and solar (10%), Fuel oil/gas (30%)
tourism: Over 2.8 million international visitors exploring Tikal National Park (epic Maya pyramids in Petén jungle), Lake Atitlán, colonial Antigua Guatemala, and Semuc Champey.
employment: Over 35% in agriculture; expanding service and manufacturing sectors; substantial diaspora remittances.
debtInflation: Monetary policy disciplined by Banco de Guatemala; low public debt to GDP ratio among Latin American nations.
transport: Carretera Panamericana (CA-1); Atlantic Highway (CA-9); Transmetro bus rapid transit in Guatemala City.
airports: La Aurora International Airport (GUA in Guatemala City)
ports: Port of Santo Tomás de Castilla and Puerto Barrios (Caribbean)
cuisine: Pepián (UNESCO national culinary heritage: rich spiced meat stew with roasted squash seeds and chili), Kak'ik (traditional Q'eqchi' turkey soup with cobanero chili), Hilachas, Tamales colorados, Rellenitos de plátano, Atol de elote, Gourmet Antigua coffee.
festivals: Semana Santa en Antigua Guatemala (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage - world's most elaborate Holy Week processions and dyed sawdust carpets)
Festival de Barriletes Gigantes (Giant Kites of Sumpango on Day of the Dead)
Fiesta de Santo Tomás in Chichicastenango
music: Marimba (national instrument, declared national cultural symbol), Traditional Maya flutes and drums, Son guatemalteco, Pop (Ricardo Arjona, Gaby Moreno - Grammy winner).
dance: Danza del Venado (Deer Dance), Danza de la Conquista, Rabinal Achí (pre-Columbian Maya dance drama).
art: Exquisite handwoven Mayan textiles (each village has distinct huipil patterns), Carlos Mérida (modernist master), Comalapa naive oil paintings.
architecture: Monumental Maya pyramids of Tikal (Temple I & IV); Spanish baroque colonial architecture and cobblestone streets in Antigua Guatemala (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
literature: Miguel Ángel Asturias (Nobel Prize in Literature 1967, El Señor Presidente, Hombres de maíz); Popol Vuh (sacred K'iche' Maya creation narrative).
cinema: Jayro Bustamante (La Llorona, Ixcanul - Golden Bear nominee, Venice award winner).
sports: Football (Estadio Doroteo Guamuch Flores), Athletics (Erick Barrondo Olympic silver medalist race walking 2012; Adriana Ruano historic first Olympic Gold medal in trap shooting at Paris 2024).
media: Prensa Libre, El Periódico, Guatevisión, Emisoras Unidas.
clothing: Traditional Maya Traje: intricately handwoven Huipil blouses, Corte wrap skirts, and Fajas sashes, worn daily by millions of indigenous women.
crafts: Backstrap-loom woven textiles, jade carving (Guatemalan jadeite from Motagua Valley), hand-painted ceramics, carved wooden masks.
worldHeritageSites: Tikal National Park (first mixed cultural/natural UNESCO site 1979)
Antigua Guatemala
Archaeological Park and Ruins of Quiriguá
National Archaeological Park Tak'alik Ab'aj (inscribed 2023)
unescoIntangible: Holy Week in Guatemala (Semana Santa)
Rabinal Achí dance drama tradition
flagDescription: Vertical triband of two celestial blue stripes (representing the Pacific and Atlantic oceans) flanking a central white stripe with the national coat of arms in the center.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features two crossed rifles and crossed swords behind a scroll reading 'LIBERTAD 15 DE SETIEMBRE DE 1821', on which perches the resplendent quetzal bird, encircled by laurel wreaths.

symbols.flower: Monja Blanca (White nun orchid - Lycaste virginalis)
symbols.tree: Ceiba pentandra (Sacred tree of the Maya)

travelNotes: The heart of the Maya world; rich indigenous living culture, dramatic volcanic beauty, and colorful textiles.
shortSummary: Guatemala is the ancient heartland of the Maya civilization, celebrated for the towering pyramids of Tikal rising above the Petén jungle, the volcanic majesty of Lake Atitlán, vibrant living indigenous traditions, and Nobel literature.

name: Haiti
motto: L'Union fait la force (Unity Makes Strength)
climate: Tropical semi-arid to humid; two rainy seasons (April–June and August–October)
biodiversity: Host to Pic Macaya National Park cloud forests, endemic frog species, and historic mangrove wetlands
government: Unitary semi-presidential republic (under Transitional Presidential Council)
latestElections: Transitional roadmap targeting general elections; international security mission deployed
politicalSituation: Governance under Transitional Presidential Council and Prime Minister Alix Didier Fils-Aimé, supported by UN-authorized Multinational Security Support (MSS) mission led by Kenya to stabilize Port-au-Prince.
foreignRelations: Founding member of UN; member of CARICOM, Francophonie, OAS, CELAC; close relations with African and Caribbean partner states.
military: Armed Forces of Haiti (FAd'H) and Haitian National Police (PNH), supported by international security forces.
history: Inhabited by the Taíno who called the land Ayiti ('Land of High Mountains'). Columbus claimed the island for Spain in 1492. Western third ceded to France in 1697 as Saint-Domingue, becoming the wealthiest colony in the world producing sugar and coffee through the brutal enslavement of hundreds of thousands of Africans. The historic 1791 slave rebellion sparked by the Bois Caïman ceremony led by Toussaint Louverture, Jean-Jacques Dessalines, and Henri Christophe culminated in victory over Napoleon's army at the Battle of Vertières (1803). On January 1, 1804, Haiti proclaimed independence, becoming the world's first independent Black republic and the first nation to abolish slavery permanently.
recentEvents2020_2026: Established Transitional Presidential Council in early 2024; deployed UN-backed Multinational Security Support mission led by Kenyan police; advanced security stabilization and preparations for general elections; celebrated 220 years of independence.
education: Université d'État d'Haïti (UEH) in Port-au-Prince and public/private institutions; expanding Creole instruction.
healthcare: Hospital of the State University of Haiti (HUEH) and NGO medical health facilities (Partners In Health / Zanmi Lasante at Mirebalais Hospital).
socialCustoms: Drinking Soup Joumou on New Year's Day (celebrating emancipation), vibrant Rara street processions during Lent, communal agricultural work (Kombit).
etiquette: Respectful French/Creole greetings ('Bonjou', 'Bonswa'), shaking hands, deep respect for family elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by pride in being the first Black republic, abolishing slavery, monumental mountain citadel architecture, and rich vibrant visual arts.
industries: Apparel assembly and textiles (HOPE/HELP US trade acts)
Sugar refining and rum distilling (Rhum Barbancourt)
agriculture: Vetiver grass (world's top producer of vetiver essential oil for luxury perfumery)
energy: Péligre hydroelectric plant (47 MW), thermal fuel generators, expanding solar micro-grids
tourism: Historic wonders including the Citadelle Laferrière and Sans-Souci Palace (UNESCO World Heritage Site), Labadee cruise destination, Jacmel arts festival, and Bassin Bleu waterfalls.
employment: Over 50% in smallholder agriculture; apparel maquiladoras; substantial diaspora remittances.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic stabilization supported by international financial institutions and remittance inflows.
transport: Route Nationale 1 and 2; colorful Tap-tap buses (custom-painted public transport vehicles adorned with religious and pop-art murals).
airports: Toussaint Louverture International Airport (PAP in Port-au-Prince)
cuisine: Soup Joumou (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage: traditional pumpkin and beef soup consumed on Independence Day), Griot (marinated fried pork chunks with spicy pikliz pickled cabbage relish), Diri ak djon djon (black mushroom rice), Legim, Akra, Rhum Barbancourt (distilled from pure sugar cane juice since 1862).
festivals: Independence Day (January 1 - Soup Joumou day)
Carnival of Jacmel (famous for papier-mâché masks)
Rara festivals during Lent
Gede (Ancestors' Day / All Saints' Day)
music: Kompa (Compas direct - popularized by Nemours Jean-Baptiste), Rasin (roots music), Rara, Mizik rasin, Rap kreyòl.
dance: Yanvalou (sacred Vodou snake dance), Ibo, Kompa, Mereng.
art: World-famous Haitian naive and intuitive painting movement (Centre d'Art: Hector Hyppolite, Philomé Obin), metal cut-out sculptures of Noailles (Croix-des-Bouquets).
architecture: Citadelle Laferrière (colossal early 19th-century mountaintop fortress, largest in the Western Hemisphere); Palais Sans-Souci; gingerbread houses in Port-au-Prince.
literature: Jacques Roumain (Gouverneurs de la Rosée), Edwidge Danticat (Breath, Eyes, Memory, The Dew Breaker), René Depestre, Dany Laferrière (member of the Académie Française).
cinema: Raoul Peck (Oscar-nominated documentary filmmaker: I Am Not Your Negro, Lumumba).
sports: Football (national passion; historic 1974 FIFA World Cup appearance; Women's national team qualified for 2023 FIFA Women's World Cup).
media: Le Nouvelliste (founded 1898, oldest French newspaper in the Americas), Radio Télévision Nationale d'Haïti (RTNH), Radio Caraïbes.
