clothing: Karabela denim and blue cotton dresses with red embroidery; linen guayaberas; colorful Tap-tap inspired casual wear.
crafts: Hand-chiseled recycled steel drum sculptures (fer découpé of Noailles), papier-mâché masks from Jacmel, carved wooden mortars.
worldHeritageSites: National History Park – Citadel, Sans Souci, Ramiers (including Citadelle Laferrière and Palace of Sans-Souci)
unescoIntangible: Joumou soup knowledge, practices and traditions (inscribed on UNESCO Representative List 2021)
flagDescription: Horizontal bicolour of blue and red, defaced with a central white square containing the national coat of arms featuring a palm tree topped by a Phrygian cap of liberty, flanked by cannons and flags.
coatOfArmsDescription: A royal palm tree topped by the Phrygian cap of liberty, flanked by trophies of cannons, bayonets, bugles, and six national flags, resting on a green lawn with a drum, over the motto 'L'UNION FAIT LA FORCE'.
landmarks: Iron Market (Marché en Fer in Port-au-Prince)
travelNotes: Rich cultural resilience and unparalleled historic monuments; travel with verified local transport and guided cultural tours.
shortSummary: Haiti is the historic vanguard of human liberation, celebrated as the world's first independent Black republic, home to the colossal mountaintop Citadelle Laferrière, UNESCO-recognized Soup Joumou, and world-renowned visionary art.
sources: Institut Haïtien de Statistique et d'Informatique (IHSI)

name: Honduras
motto: Libre, Soberana e Independiente (Free, Sovereign and Independent)
climate: Subtropical in highlands; tropical humid in Caribbean lowlands and Bay Islands
naturalHazards: Hurricanes and flash flooding (e.g., Hurricane Mitch, Eta/Iota)
biodiversity: Home to the Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve (UNESCO), the Bay Islands coral barrier reef, jaguars, and scarlet macaws
latestElections: General election 2021; general election scheduled late 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Administration of President Xiomara Castro (first female president of Honduras); focus on agrarian reform, social programs, energy renegotiation, and expanding diplomatic ties.
foreignRelations: Member of SICA, UN, OAS, CELAC; established formal diplomatic relations with China in 2023.
military: Armed Forces of Honduras (Army, Navy, Air Force) and Military Police of Public Order (PMOP).
history: Inhabited by Maya, Lenca, and Tolupan peoples. Copán flourished as a major classic Maya center known for exquisite hieroglyphic stairways and carved stelae. Conquered by Spain in the 1520s, with indigenous Lenca chief Lempira leading heroic resistance. Gained independence in 1821 from Spain. Francisco Morazán led the Federal Republic of Central America in the 1830s. The early 20th century was dominated by US banana multinationals (United Fruit, Standard Fruit). Survived 1969 Football War with El Salvador; returned to constitutional civilian democracy in 1982.
recentEvents2020_2026: President Xiomara Castro assumed presidency in 2022; concluded major trade and investment agreements with China; expanded Palmerola International Airport.
historicalFigures: Berta Cáceres (Environmental martyr and Goldman Prize winner)
education: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Honduras (UNAH in Tegucigalpa and regional centers) and Zamorano Pan-American Agricultural School.
healthcare: Hospital Escuela in Tegucigalpa and Mario Catarino Rivas Hospital in San Pedro Sula; IHSS social security health system.
socialCustoms: Eating baleadas at street stands, Sunday family soccer, Garifuna drumming celebrations on the north coast.
etiquette: Courteous, polite greetings, respectful use of titles ('Licenciado/Don'), hospitable family-oriented culture.
nationalIdentity: Defined by pride in Copán Maya archaeology, the warrior spirit of Lempira, Bay Islands scuba diving, and world-class specialty coffee.
industries: Apparel and automotive wire harness manufacturing (maquila in San Pedro Sula)
Coffee processing (#1 coffee producer in Central America, #5 globally)
Tourism and scuba diving in Bay Islands
agriculture: Highland Arabica coffee (#1 in Central America)
energy: Over 65% renewable: Hydroelectric (El Cajón Dam), Solar (Choluteca solar farms), Geothermal, Biomass, and thermal fuel
tourism: Over 2.2 million visitors enjoying Roatán and Utila in the Bay Islands (world's cheapest and top scuba certification destination), Copán Maya Ruins, Lake Yojoa, and Pico Bonito National Park.
employment: Over 30% in agriculture; expanding maquiladora manufacturing and tourism jobs; substantial diaspora remittances.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic framework supported by IMF stand-by arrangements; Central Bank of Honduras manages currency crawling peg.
transport: CA-5 highway connecting Tegucigalpa to San Pedro Sula; Palmerola airport expressway; inter-island ferries to Roatán.
airports: Ramón Villeda Morales International (SAP in San Pedro Sula)
Juan Manuel Gálvez International (RTB on Roatán)
ports: Puerto Cortés (deepwater modern container port, leading port in Central America)
cuisine: Baleadas (warm handmade thick flour tortilla folded with refried red beans, crumbled hard cheese / queso duro, and mantequilla cream; often added eggs, avocado, or steak), Sopa de caracol (conch soup in coconut milk, celebrated in famous Banda Blanca song), Tamales nacatamales, Yuca con chicharrón, Pastelitos de carne, Copán coffee.
festivals: Feria Isidra and Gran Carnaval Nacional in La Ceiba (May)
Semana Santa (Holy Week sawdust carpets in Comayagua)
Day of the Garifuna (April 12)
music: Punta (Garifuna drums and turtle shells), Marimba, Sopa de Caracol (Banda Blanca international hit), Folkloric dance tunes.
dance: Punta dance, Danza de las Guancasco, traditional Lenca folk dances.
art: Copán intricate Maya stone carvings, Lenca pottery from Guajiquiro, naive paintings of José Antonio Velásquez.
architecture: Copán Hieroglyphic Stairway (longest inscribed Maya text in the world); Spanish colonial architecture in Comayagua (home to the oldest working clock in the Americas, c. 1100 CE).
literature: Ramón Amaya Amador (Prisión Verde), Lucila Gamero de Medina (Blanca Olmedo), Roberto Sosa (Cervantes honor poet).
cinema: Amor y Frijoles, A Place in the Caribbean; acclaimed wildlife conservation documentaries.
sports: Football (passionate national sport; 3-time FIFA World Cup appearances; Olimpia and Motagua rivalry), Baseball, Scuba diving.
media: La Prensa, El Heraldo, Proceso Digital, HCH Televisión Digital, Televicentro.
clothing: Traditional white cotton traje criollo with colorful embroidery; modern casual western attire.
crafts: Lenca black and white pottery, carved Maya wooden replicas, hand-rolled cigars from Danlí, woven pine needle baskets.
worldHeritageSites: Maya Site of Copán (renowned for exquisite high-relief sculptures and hieroglyphic stairway)
Río Plátano Biosphere Reserve
unescoIntangible: Language, dance and music of the Garifuna (shared with Belize, Guatemala, Nicaragua)
flagDescription: Horizontal triband of turquoise blue, white, and turquoise blue, with five turquoise five-pointed stars arranged in an X-pattern in the center representing the five nations of the former Federal Republic of Central America.
coatOfArmsDescription: An equilateral triangle showing two castles, a rainbow, a rising sun between two oceans, surrounded by an oval inscribed 'REPÚBLICA DE HONDURAS, LIBRE, SOBERANA E INDEPENDIENTE', crowned by a quiver of arrows and cornucopias, resting on oak and pine trees with mining tools.
travelNotes: World's most affordable PADI scuba diving certification in Utila; ancient Maya high art in Copán; warm Catracho hospitality.
shortSummary: Honduras is Central America's coffee and archaeological powerhouse, home to the breathtaking Maya hieroglyphic stairways of Copán, the vibrant diving paradise of the Bay Islands, and the irresistible flavors of the baleada.

name: Jamaica
motto: Out of Many, One People
climate: Tropical maritime with constant ocean trade winds
naturalHazards: Hurricanes and storm surges (Atlantic hurricane season)
biodiversity: Home to the Blue and John Crow Mountains (UNESCO), Jamaican swallowtail (largest butterfly in the Americas), and indigenous Doctor Bird
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Sir Patrick Allen)
legislature: Parliament of Jamaica (Senate and House of Representatives)
latestElections: General election 2020; local government 2024; general election scheduled 2025
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Andrew Holness leading economic expansion, record low unemployment, debt reduction, and ongoing constitutional review toward transitioning to a republic.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; globally celebrated cultural diplomacy through music, athletics, and tourism.
military: Jamaica Defence Force (JDF: Jamaica Regiment, JDF Air Wing, JDF Coast Guard).
history: Inhabited by the Taíno who named the island Xaymaca ('Land of Wood and Water'). Columbus arrived in 1494. Spanish rule ceded to Britain in 1655 under Oliver Cromwell's forces. Sugar plantations powered by enslaved Africans made Jamaica Britain's most valuable colony. Escaped Africans formed independent Maroon communities in the Cockpit Country, waging successful guerrilla wars against the British to secure autonomy in the 1739 treaty under Queen Nanny. Sam Sharpe led the 1831 Baptist War that accelerated British abolition of slavery in 1834. Achieved independence on August 6, 1962 under Sir Alexander Bustamante.
recentEvents2020_2026: Achieved historic economic debt-to-GDP reduction below 75%; reached record-breaking tourism arrivals exceeding 4.3 million visitors; advanced parliamentary constitutional commission on republican transition.
historicalFigures: Queen Nanny of the Maroons (National Hero)
Marcus Garvey (Pan-African leader and National Hero)
religions: Protestant (Church of God ~24%, Seventh-day Adventist ~12%, Baptist ~7%, Pentecostal ~8%) ~65%
education: University of the West Indies (UWI) Mona Campus (founding campus, premier research center in the Caribbean) and University of Technology (UTech).
healthcare: University Hospital of the West Indies and Kingston Public Hospital provide major regional medical care.
socialCustoms: Sound system street dances, playing dominoes, drinking Blue Mountain coffee, Rastafarian Ital cuisine and philosophy.
etiquette: Expressive, rhythmic Patois greeting ('Wah Gwaan?'), polite respect for elders, warm hospitality.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated worldwide for Reggae music, the spiritual philosophy of Bob Marley, sprinting dominance (fastest humans on Earth), and Jerk cooking.
sectors: Tourism & Hospitality 55%, Services & BPO 25%, Bauxite & Manufacturing 12%, Agriculture 8%
industries: Rum distilling (Appleton Estate, J. Wray & Nephew)
agriculture: Blue Mountain coffee (one of the world's most sought-after coffees)
naturalResources: Pristine white sand beaches (Seven Mile Beach)
energy: Over 20% renewable energy penetration via Wigton Windfarm, Paradise Park Solar, and hydroelectric plants, backed by LNG and fuel oil
tourism: Over 4.3 million international stopover and cruise travelers flocking to Montego Bay, Negril Seven Mile Beach, Dunn's River Falls in Ocho Rios, Port Antonio, and the Bob Marley Museum in Kingston.
employment: Unemployment historically low at approx. 4.2%; booming employment in tourism, construction, and tech outsourcing.
debtInflation: Bank of Jamaica successfully maintains inflation within 4-6% target band; remarkable multi-year fiscal debt consolidation.
transport: Highway 2000 toll network connecting Kingston, Montego Bay, and Ocho Rios; scenic coastal highways.
airports: Sangster International Airport (MBJ in Montego Bay - Caribbean's busiest tourist airport)
ports: Port of Kingston (world-class container transshipment hub on seventh-largest natural harbor in the world)
Ocho Rios and Falmouth Cruise Ports
cuisine: Ackee and Saltfish (national dish: sauteed salted cod with boiled ackee fruit, peppers, onions, and spices), Jerk chicken and Jerk pork (smoked over sweet pimento wood), Jamaican beef patties (golden flaky turmeric pastry with spiced beef), Curry goat with rice and peas, Escovitch fish, Bammy, Blue Mountain coffee, Appleton Estate rum.
festivals: Reggae Sumfest (Montego Bay in July - world's premier reggae music festival)
Jamaica Carnival (Bacchanal)
Bob Marley Week (February)
Calabash International Literary Festival
music: Reggae (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Ska, Rocksteady, Dancehall, Dub, Mento, Nyabinghi drumming.
dance: Dancehall street dancing (bogle, dutty wine), Kumina ancestral dance, Ska skank.
art: Edna Manley (Mother of Jamaican Art, famed sculptor), Mallica 'Kapo' Reynolds (intuitive master), Barrington Watson, National Gallery of Jamaica.
architecture: Devon House (classic Jamaican Georgian architecture in Kingston); historic Spanish Town square; bohemian cliffside hotels in Negril.
literature: Claude McKay (Harlem Renaissance master poet), Roger Mais, Marlon James (Booker Prize winner for A Brief History of Seven Killings), Lorna Goodison (Poet Laureate).
cinema: The Harder They Come (starring Jimmy Cliff - introduced reggae and Jamaican culture to the world), Cool Runnings (celebrating the 1988 Jamaican bobsled team).
sports: Track and Field (undisputed global sprinting superpower: Usain Bolt - world record holder in 100m and 200m; Shelly-Ann Fraser-Pryce; Elaine Thompson-Herah; Veronica Campbell-Brown; Asafa Powell), Cricket (Sabina Park), Football (Reggae Boyz, Reggae Girlz).
media: The Gleaner (founded 1834, one of the oldest newspapers in the Americas), Jamaica Observer, TVJ (Television Jamaica), CVM TV.
clothing: Vibrant green, gold, and red Rastafarian tam hats; lightweight linen clothing; colorful carnival costumes.
holidays: National Heroes Day (Third Monday in October)
crafts: Carved lignum vitae and cedar wood statues, woven wicker baskets, jipijapa straw hats, pottery.
worldHeritageSites: Blue and John Crow Mountains (mixed cultural and natural World Heritage Site, refuge for the Maroons)
unescoIntangible: Reggae music of Jamaica (inscribed on UNESCO Representative List 2018)
flagDescription: A diagonal yellow cross (saltire) divides the flag into four triangles: green (top and bottom, symbolizing agricultural hope and lush vegetation) and black (hoist and fly, symbolizing hardship overcome). Unique as the only national flag that does not share any colors with the flags of the USA, UK, or France (no red, white, or blue).
coatOfArmsDescription: Features a Taíno woman holding a basket of fruit and a Taíno man holding a bow, flanking a shield with a red cross bearing five golden pineapples, crowned by an American crocodile on a royal helmet, over the motto 'OUT OF MANY, ONE PEOPLE'.
landmarks: Negril Seven Mile Beach & Rick's Café
travelNotes: Vibrant, world-famous cultural and beach haven; extraordinary musical energy, warm hospitality, and iconic jerk cuisine.
shortSummary: Jamaica is a cultural giant of the Caribbean, world-renowned as the birthplace of Reggae music and Bob Marley, the home of the world's fastest Olympic sprinters, the lush Blue Mountains, and savory Jerk cooking.

name: Mexico
nativeName: Estados Unidos Mexicanos / Mēxihcatl Tlacetilīlli Tlahtohcāyōtl
motto: None (historic: La Patria es Primero)
longestRiver: Rio Grande / Río Bravo (3,034 km border) / Balsas River
climate: Arid to semi-arid in the northern deserts, temperate in high central plateaus, tropical wet-and-dry in southern lowlands and Yucatán
naturalHazards: Major earthquakes (Guerrero and Cocos subduction zone)
Hurricanes on Pacific and Atlantic coasts
environmentalIssues: Air quality in Mexico City valley
Water scarcity in northern industrial centers
biodiversity: One of the world's top 5 megadiverse countries; holds 10-12% of the world's biodiversity, home to monarch butterflies, jaguars, and vaquita porpoises
timeZone: UTC-08:00 to UTC-05:00 (four main time zones)
languages: 68 recognized indigenous languages (Nahuatl, Maya, Zapotec, Mixtec, Otomi, Tzeltal)
legislature: Congress of the Union (Senate of the Republic and Chamber of Deputies)
latestElections: General election June 2024 (historic landslide electing Claudia Sheinbaum as first female president)
politicalSituation: Inauguration of President Claudia Sheinbaum in October 2024; execution of landmark judicial reform, expansion of passenger rail, nearshoring industrial boom, and renewable energy investments.
foreignRelations: Member of G20, OECD, USMCA, Pacific Alliance, UN, OAS, APEC; leading diplomatic bridge between North America and Latin America.
military: Mexican Armed Forces (Secretariat of National Defense / Army and Air Force; Secretariat of the Navy) and National Guard.
history: Cradle of monumental Mesoamerican civilizations: Olmec ('mother culture'), Teotihuacan, Maya, Toltec, Zapotec, and the Aztec Empire (Tenochtitlan, founded 1325). Hernán Cortés led the Spanish conquest in 1521, establishing the Viceroyalty of New Spain. Father Miguel Hidalgo launched the War of Independence with the Grito de Dolores on September 16, 1810; independence achieved in 1821. Benito Juárez defended the republic and defeated French intervention in the 1860s. The Mexican Revolution (1910–1920) led by Francisco Madero, Emiliano Zapata, and Pancho Villa established modern social rights and land reform.
recentEvents2020_2026: Elected Dr. Claudia Sheinbaum as the first female president in Mexican history in June 2024; completed the Maya Train (Tren Maya) circling the Yucatán Peninsula and the Interoceanic Corridor of the Isthmus of Tehuantepec; capitalized on massive nearshoring manufacturing investments.
historicalFigures: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz
ethnicGroups: Indigenous ~21.5% (identifying as indigenous by culture and language)
education: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de México (UNAM - UNESCO World Heritage campus, leading university in Latin America) and Tecnológico de Monterrey (ITESM).
healthcare: IMSS (Mexican Social Security Institute), ISSSTE, and IMSS-Bienestar providing universal healthcare coverage to non-salaried citizens.
socialCustoms: Día de los Muertos (Day of the Dead - honoring ancestors with cempasúchil flowers and ofrendas), Sunday family meals with barbacoa, lucha libre wrestling matches, mariachi serenades.
etiquette: Warm, respectful, greeting with polite handshakes or light hugs, using 'Usted' with elders, deep hospitality ('Mi casa es su casa').
nationalIdentity: Defined by the profound syncretism of ancient Mesoamerican civilizations and Spanish heritage, celebrated globally for cuisine, art, Mariachi music, and vibrant colors.
industries: Automotive manufacturing (world's #4 vehicle exporter, #1 in Latin America)
Electronics and computer manufacturing (Guadalajara Silicon Valley)
naturalResources: Breathtaking Pacific, Caribbean, and Gulf beaches
energy: Natural gas (58%), Hydroelectric (14%), Solar and wind (12%), Petroleum (8%), Geothermal (4%), Nuclear (Laguna Verde - 4%)
tradePartners: United States (largest partner, over 80% of exports; Mexico is the #1 trading partner of the US)
tourism: Over 45 million international travelers (top 6 most visited countries in the world), enjoying Cancún, Riviera Maya, Mexico City, Los Cabos, Puerto Vallarta, Oaxaca, and San Miguel de Allende.
employment: Unemployment historically low at approx. 2.7%; booming nearshoring industrial manufacturing and tech.
debtInflation: Strong fiscal discipline; Bank of Mexico (Banxico) maintains autonomous inflation targeting; 'Super Peso' resilience.
transport: Extensive highway network (Autopistas); newly completed Tren Maya (1,554 km tourist and freight railway); Interoceanic Corridor rail; Mexico City Metro and Metrobús.
ports: Port of Manzanillo (Pacific's busiest container hub)
cuisine: Traditional Mexican Cuisine (inscribed on UNESCO Representative List of Intangible Cultural Heritage): Tacos (al pastor, carnitas, barbacoa), Mole poblano and Mole oaxaqueño (complex rich sauces with chilis, chocolate, and spices), Pozole, Enchiladas, Tamales, Chiles en nogada, Guacamole, Tequila and Mezcal.
festivals: Día de los Muertos (November 1–2 - UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage)
Guelaguetza in Oaxaca (July)
Grito de Dolores / Independence Day (September 15–16)
Cervantino International Festival (Guanajuato)
Guadalajara International Book Fair (FIL - world's largest Spanish book fair)
music: Mariachi (UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage), Ranchera (Vicente Fernández), Son jarocho, Banda sinaloense, Corridos tumbados (Peso Pluma), Mexican rock (Caifanes, Maná), Bolero.
dance: Jarabe Tapatío (Mexican Hat Dance - national folk dance), Danza de los Voladores (Papantla Flyers - UNESCO), Danza del Venado.
art: Frida Kahlo (global feminist art icon), Diego Rivera, David Alfaro Siqueiros, José Clemente Orozco (The Great Mexican Muralists), Rufino Tamayo, Leonora Carrington.
architecture: Ancient pyramids (Teotihuacan's Pyramid of the Sun, Chichen Itza's El Castillo - New 7 Wonders of the World); colonial baroque in Puebla and Oaxaca; modern masterpieces of Luis Barragán (Pritzker Prize winner).
literature: Octavio Paz (Nobel Prize in Literature 1990, The Labyrinth of Solitude), Carlos Fuentes, Juan Rulfo (Pedro Páramo), Elena Poniatowska, Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz.
cinema: The 'Three Amigos' (three-time/four-time Academy Award-winning directors: Alfonso Cuarón, Guillermo del Toro, Alejandro González Iñárritu); Golden Age of Mexican Cinema (Pedro Infante, María Félix, Cantinflas).
sports: Football (Estadio Azteca - first stadium to host three FIFA World Cups: 1970, 1986, 2026), Boxing (legendary world champions: Julio César Chávez, Canelo Álvarez), Lucha Libre (masked professional wrestling: El Santo, Blue Demon), Formula 1 (Sergio 'Checo' Pérez; Mexico City Grand Prix).
media: TelevisaUnivision, TV Azteca, El Universal, Reforma, La Jornada, Milenio.
clothing: Traje de Charro (elaborate formal equestrian suit), Huipil and Rebozo shawls, Guayabera shirts.
holidays: December 12 (Day of the Virgin of Guadalupe)
May 5 (Cinco de Mayo / Battle of Puebla)
crafts: Talavera ceramics from Puebla (UNESCO), Oaxacan alebrijes (carved fantastical wooden creatures), Huichol yarn and bead art, barro negro pottery.
worldHeritageSites: Historic Centre of Mexico City and Xochimilco
Pre-Hispanic City of Teotihuacan
Pre-Hispanic City and National Park of Palenque
Pre-Hispanic City of Chichen-Itza
Historic Town of Guanajuato
Agave Landscape and Ancient Industrial Facilities of Tequila
unescoIntangible: Indigenous festivity dedicated to the dead (Día de los Muertos)
Traditional Mexican cuisine
Mariachi, string music, song and trumpet
Ritual ceremony of the Voladores
flagDescription: Vertical tricolor of green (hope), white (unity), and red (blood of national heroes), charged in the center of the white stripe with the national coat of arms depicting an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus devouring a rattlesnake.
coatOfArmsDescription: A Mexican golden eagle perched on a nopal cactus growing out of a rock rising from a lake, grasping a rattlesnake in its talon and beak, encircled by oak and laurel branches tied with a tricolor ribbon.
landmarks: Teotihuacan Pyramids of the Sun and Moon
Historic Centre of Mexico City & Zócalo
travelNotes: One of the world's supreme cultural, gastronomic, and archaeological destinations; rich regional diversities across all 32 federal entities.
shortSummary: Mexico is a cultural titan of the Americas, boasting the ancient wonders of Teotihuacan and Chichen Itza, the world-renowned culinary heritage of tacos and mole, the vibrant tradition of Día de los Muertos, and a booming modern industrial economy.
sources: Instituto Nacional de Estadística y Geografía (INEGI México)

name: Nicaragua
motto: En Dios Confiamos (In God We Trust)
longestRiver: Coco River / Río Segovia (750 km border with Honduras)
majorLakes: Lake Nicaragua / Cocibolca (largest lake in Central America, home to freshwater sharks)
climate: Tropical in lowlands, cooler in central highlands; dry season November to April; wet season May to October
biodiversity: Largest country in Central America; home to Bosawás Biosphere Reserve (second largest rainforest in the Americas), freshwater bull sharks in Lake Cocibolca, and volcanic island of Ometepe
headOfGovernment: President Daniel Ortega / Vice President Rosario Murillo
latestElections: General election 2021; municipal 2022; general election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: FSLN governance under President Daniel Ortega and Vice President Rosario Murillo; major diplomatic alignment with China and Russia; expanding Free Trade Agreement with China.
foreignRelations: Member of ALBA, SICA, UN, CELAC; formal diplomatic ties with the People's Republic of China since 2021.
military: Nicaraguan Armed Forces (Army, Navy, Air Force) and National Police.
adminDivisions: 15 departments and 2 autonomous regions (RACCN and RACCS)
history: Inhabited by Nicarao, Chorotega, and Miskito peoples. Spanish arrived in 1522; Francisco Hernández de Córdoba founded the historic colonial cities of Granada and León in 1524. Gained independence in 1821 from Spain. In the 1850s, US filibuster William Walker briefly seized the country before being defeated by allied Central American armies. The 20th century was shaped by Augusto C. Sandino's resistance against US occupation, followed by the Somoza dynasty dictatorship (1936–1979). The Sandinista Revolution overthrew Somoza in 1979, leading to the Contra War in the 1980s until democratic elections in 1990.
recentEvents2020_2026: Enacted full Free Trade Agreement with the People's Republic of China in 2024; expanded solar, geothermal, and wind grid capacity to over 70% renewable generation.
historicalFigures: Rubén Darío (Father of Modernismo in Spanish literature)
Violeta Barrios de Chamorro (First female president in the Americas, 1990)
education: Universidad Nacional Autónoma de Nicaragua (UNAN in León and Managua); free public primary and secondary education.
healthcare: Universal public health network operated by MINSA (Ministry of Health) with new regional hospitals in León, Chinandega, and Bilwi.
socialCustoms: Celebration of La Purísima (December 7 - Gritería honoring the Immaculate Conception), street theatrical performances of El Güegüense, sharing Gallo Pinto.
etiquette: Courteous greetings, polite handshakes, respectful conversational tone, warm family hospitality.
nationalIdentity: Defined by pride as the 'Land of Lakes and Volcanoes', poetic devotion to Rubén Darío, freshwater sharks of Lake Cocibolca, and rich theatrical satire.
energy: Over 70% renewable: Geothermal (San Jacinto-Tizate, Momotombo), Wind (Rivas wind corridor), Hydroelectric, Biomass, and solar
tradePartners: Central American neighbours (El Salvador, Costa Rica)
tourism: Over 1.5 million visitors exploring colonial Granada (oldest city on the American mainland in its original site), Ometepe Island (twin volcanoes in a freshwater lake), Corn Islands, and volcano boarding down Cerro Negro.
employment: Over 30% in agriculture; expanding free-zone manufacturing and tourism hospitality.
debtInflation: Exchange rate stabilized by Central Bank of Nicaragua (crawling peg adjusted to 0% annual crawl in 2024); strong remittance inflows.
transport: Carretera Panamericana (CA-1); modern paved highway connecting the Pacific to Bluefields on the Caribbean coast.
airports: Augusto C. Sandino International Airport (MGA in Managua)
ports: Port of Corinto (Pacific deepwater cargo gateway)
Port of San Juan del Sur
cuisine: Gallo Pinto (fried rice and red silk beans), Nacatamal (large corn dough parcel stuffed with seasoned pork, rice, potatoes, and prunes, wrapped in plantain leaves), Vigorón (boiled yuca topped with crispy chicharrón and curtido salad on a banana leaf), Quesillo, Indio Viejo, Flor de Caña rum (world-renowned carbon-neutral rum).
festivals: La Gritería / La Purísima (December 7 - nationwide celebration shouting '¿Quién causa tanta alegría? ¡La Concepción de María!')
Fiesta de Santo Domingo de Guzmán (Managua in August)
Palo de Mayo (Maypole festival in Bluefields)
music: Marimba de arco (wooden marimba played with mallets), Son nica, Chicheros (brass marching bands), Palo de Mayo Afro-Caribbean music, Carlos Mejía Godoy.
dance: El Güegüense satirical dance, Danza de las Inditas, Palo de Mayo dance.
art: Solentiname Islands primitivist painting movement (founded by Ernesto Cardenal on Lake Nicaragua), San Juan de Oriente polychrome ceramics.
architecture: Colonial architecture in Granada and León; historic León Cathedral (largest cathedral in Central America - UNESCO World Heritage Site, burial place of Rubén Darío).
literature: Rubén Darío (revolutionary founder of the Modernismo movement that transformed all Spanish-language literature: Azul..., Cantos de vida y esperanza), Ernesto Cardenal, Gioconda Belli, Sergio Ramírez (Cervantes Prize winner).
cinema: Documentaries on the Sandinista Revolution and poetry festivals; thriving local indie short-film community.
sports: Baseball (the undisputed national sport; produced MLB legends: Dennis Martínez - threw a perfect game in 1991; Jonathan Loáisiga), Boxing (legendary 3-division world champions: Alexis Argüello, Roman 'Chocolatito' González).
media: El 19 Digital, Canal 4, Canal 6, Radio Ya, VosTV.
clothing: Traditional Cotona embroidered linen shirts for men; colorful folkloric dresses for women; western casual attire.
crafts: San Juan de Oriente ceramic vases and pottery, Masaya woven cotton hammocks, carved balsa wood animals from Solentiname.
worldHeritageSites: Ruins of León Viejo (early Spanish colonial city founded 1524)
León Cathedral (burial site of Rubén Darío)
unescoIntangible: El Güegüense (first literary and satirical theatrical work of post-Columbian America, inscribed 2008)
flagDescription: Horizontal triband of two cobalt blue stripes (representing the Pacific Ocean and Caribbean Sea) flanking a central white stripe with the national coat of arms in the center.
coatOfArmsDescription: An equilateral triangle showing five volcanoes between two oceans, a red Phrygian cap of liberty radiating golden light, and a rainbow, encircled by the golden inscription 'REPÚBLICA DE NICARAGUA - AMÉRICA CENTRAL'.
landmarks: Ometepe Island (Concepción & Maderas Volcanoes in Lake Cocibolca)
Granada Colonial Plaza & Islets of Granada
Masaya Volcano National Park (active glowing lava lake)
travelNotes: Land of Lakes and Volcanoes; board down active black-ash volcanoes; explore pristine Caribbean Corn Islands; extremely affordable.
shortSummary: Nicaragua is the 'Land of Lakes and Volcanoes', celebrated for the colonial elegance of Granada and León, the poetic genius of Rubén Darío, the volcanic island of Ometepe in vast Lake Cocibolca, and world-class surfing and cigars.
sources: Instituto Nacional de Información de Desarrollo (INIDE Nicaragua)

name: Panama
nationalDay: November 3 (Separation Day from Colombia) / November 28 (Independence from Spain)
motto: Pro Mundi Beneficio (For the Benefit of the World)
highestPoint: Volcán Barú (3,474 m - can view both Pacific and Atlantic on clear days)
longestRiver: Chagres River (193 km - key water source for Panama Canal) / Tuira River
majorLakes: Gatun Lake (artificial lake forming key portion of Panama Canal)
climate: Tropical maritime; prolonged rainy season (May to December) and short dry season (January to April)
environmentalIssues: Watershed deforestation threatening Panama Canal freshwater reservoir capacity
biodiversity: Crucial biological land bridge between North and South America; hosts more bird species than the United States and Canada combined
languages: indigenous languages: Ngäbere, Guna, Emberá, Buglere
currency: Panamanian Balboa (PAB, B/.) / United States Dollar (USD, $ - circulating currency, 1:1)
latestElections: General election May 2024 (José Raúl Mulino elected President)
politicalSituation: Inauguration of President José Raúl Mulino in July 2024; strategic focus on water reservoir expansion for the Panama Canal, border control in the Darién Gap, and international logistics leadership.
foreignRelations: Member of SICA, UN, OAS, CELAC; global logistics and maritime hub; close strategic alliance with the United States.
military: Abolished standing army in 1990; Panamanian Public Forces (National Police, SENAN naval/air service, SENAFRONT border service).
adminDivisions: 10 provinces and 4 indigenous comarcas (with provincial status)
history: Inhabited by indigenous Cuevas, Guna, and Chibcha peoples. Vasco Núñez de Balboa crossed the Isthmus in 1513, becoming the first European to sight the Pacific Ocean. Panama became the Spanish Empire's royal transshipment hub for Peruvian silver (Camino Real). Gained independence from Spain in 1821 and joined Gran Colombia. In 1903, backed by the United States, Panama separated from Colombia to build the Panama Canal, opened in August 1914. The Torrijos-Carter Treaties (1977) transferred full sovereignty of the Canal and the Canal Zone to Panama on December 31, 1999. In 2016, completed the historic $5.4B Panama Canal Expansion.
recentEvents2020_2026: Elected José Raúl Mulino as president in May 2024; executed multi-billion-dollar water-saving initiatives ensuring full vessel transits through the Panama Canal; opened Panama Metro Line 3 connecting western suburbs.
education: University of Panama (UP), Technological University of Panama (UTP), and City of Knowledge (Ciudad del Saber international academic park).
healthcare: Hospital Santo Tomás and CSS (Social Security Fund) hospitals alongside world-class private facilities (Hospital Punta Pacífica affiliated with Johns Hopkins).
socialCustoms: Carnaval de Las Tablas (famous rivalry between Calle Arriba and Calle Abajo), wearing Pollera dresses, drinking world-record Geisha coffee.
etiquette: Polite greetings, professional attire in business (Panama City is a major financial hub), respectful warmth in social gatherings.
nationalIdentity: Defined by its destiny as the 'Bridge of the World, Heart of the Universe', the engineering marvel of the Canal, and Indigenous Guna Mola textiles.
sectors: Logistics, Canal & Financial Services 75%, Industry & Construction 20%, Agriculture 5%
industries: Panama Canal operations and maritime services
International banking and offshore financial hub
Colon Free Trade Zone (second largest free trade zone in the world)
Aviation hub (Copa Airlines / Hub of the Americas)
agriculture: Specialty Geisha coffee (Boquete - commands world-record auction prices exceeding $10,000/kg)
energy: Over 75% renewable: Hydroelectric (Fortuna, Bayano), Solar and wind (Penonomé wind farm), backed by LNG (AES Colón)
exports: Panama Canal transit fees and maritime logistics
tourism: Over 2.9 million international visitors exploring the Panama Canal Miraflores Locks, Casco Viejo (historic colonial quarter), San Blas / Guna Yala archipelago, Bocas del Toro, and Boquete coffee plantations.
employment: Logistics, banking, airline hub operations, international trade, and construction.
debtInflation: Balboa pegged 1:1 with US Dollar; stable investment-grade sovereign credit ratings.
transport: Panama Metro (Line 1, 2, and Line 3 with monorail over Panama Canal); Transisthmian highway and Panama Canal Railway.
airports: Tocumen International Airport (PTY in Panama City - 'Hub of the Americas' connecting over 85 international destinations)
ports: Port of Manzanillo and Colón Container Terminal (Caribbean entrance to Canal)
cuisine: Sancocho de gallina (national soup: hearty hen stew with yuca, corn, culantro, and herbs), Ceviche corvina in lime juice, Ropa vieja, Carimañolas (cassava fritters stuffed with spiced meat), Arroz con pollo, Hojaldras, World-famous Boquete Geisha coffee.
festivals: Carnaval de Las Tablas (splendid rival parades with queens, fireworks, and water culecos)
Festival de la Pollera (Las Tablas in July)
Festival de la Mejorana in Guararé
music: Salsa (Rubén Blades - 17-time Grammy/Latin Grammy winner), Tipico music / Cumbia panameña (Osvaldo Ayala, Samy y Sandra Sandoval), Reggaeton / Reggae en Español pioneers (El General).
dance: El Tamborito (national folk dance with African and Spanish roots), Danza de los Diablicos Sucios, Cumbia.
art: Molas (exquisite multi-layered reverse-appliqué textiles hand-sewn by indigenous Guna women), Emberá woven cocobolo wood and tagua nut carvings.
architecture: Casco Antiguo Spanish colonial mansions; modern glittering skyscraper skyline of Panama City ('Dubai of the Americas'); Biomuseo (Frank Gehry's only building in Latin America).
literature: Ricardo Miró (National Poet: Patria), Rogelio Sinán, Joaquín Beleño.
cinema: Invasion (Abner Benaim), Plaza Catedral; thriving international co-productions and film incentives.
sports: Baseball (Major League legends: Mariano Rivera - first unanimous Baseball Hall of Fame inductee; Rod Carew), Boxing (Roberto 'Manos de Piedra' Durán - 4-weight world champion), Football (national team Los Canaleros).
media: La Prensa, Panamá América, TVN (Canal 2), Telemetro (Canal 13).
clothing: La Pollera (national female dress: breathtaking hand-embroidered white lace gown worn with gold jewelry and tembleques hair ornaments, costing up to $15,000), Montuno shirt and Sombrero Pintao for men.
crafts: Guna Mola tapestries, Sombrero Pintao (handwoven palm hat - UNESCO Intangible Heritage), carved Tagua nuts ('vegetable ivory'), Emberá chunga palm baskets.
worldHeritageSites: Archaeological Site of Panamá Viejo and Historic District of Panamá (Casco Antiguo)
Fortifications on the Caribbean Side of Panama: Portobelo-San Lorenzo
Darién National Park
Coiba National Park and its Special Zone of Marine Protection
unescoIntangible: Artisanal processes and plant fibers techniques for the Sombrero Pintao (inscribed 2017)
Corpus Christi festive dances and rituals
flagDescription: Divided into four quarters: upper hoist white with a blue five-pointed star; upper fly plain red; lower hoist plain blue; lower fly white with a red five-pointed star. Represents the peaceful alternation between Conservative (blue) and Liberal (red) parties.
coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by national flags, featuring an eagle holding a scroll reading 'PRO MUNDI BENEFICIO', above a shield showing crossed rifle and sword on green, shovel and pick on red, a setting sun over the isthmus on blue, and a cornucopia and winged wheel on green, surmounted by ten golden stars.

symbols.animal: Harpy eagle (Águila harpía - world's most powerful raptor)
symbols.flower: Holy Ghost orchid (Flor del Espíritu Santo - Peristeria elata, shaped like a white dove)

landmarks: Casco Viejo (Historic District of Panama City)
Guna Yala / San Blas Islands (365 pristine Caribbean islands)
travelNotes: Crossroads of the world; high-speed metro and gleaming modern skyline; easy connection via Tocumen Airport; US dollar accepted everywhere 1:1.
shortSummary: Panama is the vital crossroads of the world, celebrated for the monumental engineering wonder of the Panama Canal connecting two oceans, the glittering skyscrapers of Panama City, indigenous Guna Molas, and world-record Geisha coffee.

name: Saint Kitts and Nevis
officialName: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
nativeName: Federation of Saint Christopher and Nevis
motto: Country Above Self
highestPoint: Mount Liamuiga (1,156 m on St. Kitts)
climate: Tropical maritime with constant ocean trade winds
naturalHazards: Hurricanes and storm surges (Atlantic hurricane season)
biodiversity: Volcanic peaks covered in pristine rainforests (dormant crater of Mount Liamuiga), coral reefs, and green vervet monkey populations
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Dame Marcella Liburd)
mainPoliticalParties: Saint Kitts and Nevis Labour Party (SKNLP)
latestElections: General election 2022; general election scheduled 2027
politicalSituation: Administration of Prime Minister Terrance Drew pioneering the 'Sustainable Island State' initiative, reforming Citizenship by Investment, and geothermal development on Nevis.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; maintains formal diplomatic ties with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
military: Saint Kitts and Nevis Defence Force (SKNDF: Coast Guard and land force).
adminDivisions: 14 parishes (9 on St. Kitts, 5 on Nevis)
history: Inhabited by Kalinago (Carib) peoples. Sighted by Columbus in 1493. English settlement led by Sir Thomas Warner in 1623 was Britain's first Caribbean colony ('The Mother Colony of the West Indies'); shared with French settlement until Treaty of Utrecht (1713). Brimstone Hill Fortress (the 'Gibraltar of the West Indies') built by enslaved labor to dominate the Caribbean sea lanes. Alexander Hamilton (US Founding Father) was born in Charlestown, Nevis in 1755 or 1757. Gained independence on September 19, 1983 under Sir Kennedy Simmonds, becoming the smallest sovereign state in the Americas.
recentEvents2020_2026: Appointed Dame Marcella Liburd as first female Governor-General; launched geothermal drilling on Nevis targeting 100% clean power; hosted Caribbean Premier League (CPL) cricket championships.
historicalFigures: Alexander Hamilton (US Founding Father, born on Nevis)
Sir Kennedy Simmonds (First Prime Minister and National Hero)
education: Clarence Fitzroy Bryant College and Ross University School of Veterinary Medicine; free compulsory basic schooling.
healthcare: Joseph N. France General Hospital in Basseterre and Alexandra Hospital in Charlestown.
socialCustoms: Sugar Mas Carnival, Friday afternoon street limes, cricket matches at Warner Park, sharing goat water stew.
etiquette: Friendly and courteous, polite greetings ('Good morning'), respect for community elders.
nationalIdentity: Defined by pride as the smallest sovereign federation in the Americas, birthplace of Alexander Hamilton, and the Gibraltar of the Caribbean at Brimstone Hill.
gdpPerCapita: $23,900 (one of the highest in the Eastern Caribbean)
sectors: Tourism & Hospitality 65%, Financial Services 18%, Construction 10%, Agriculture & Fisheries 7%
industries: Citizenship by Investment (world's oldest CIP program, founded 1984)
Beverage brewing (Carib beer) and light assembly
agriculture: Transitioned from historic monoculture sugar (closed 2005) to diversified vegetables, tropical fruits, and artisanal sea-island cotton
energy: Advancing toward 100% clean electricity via the Nevis Geothermal Project and utility-scale solar PV farms
tourism: Over 1.2 million total cruise and stayover visitors enjoying Brimstone Hill Fortress (UNESCO World Heritage), St. Kitts Scenic Railway (last operating passenger railway in the West Indies), and luxury resorts in Nevis.
employment: Tourism and hotel hospitality, public service, financial and legal services.
debtInflation: XCD pegged 2.70:1 to USD; low and predictable inflation.
transport: St. Kitts Scenic Railway (scenic double-decker tourist train circling historic sugar estates); passenger ferries connecting St. Kitts and Nevis across The Narrows.
airports: Robert L. Bradshaw International Airport (SKB in Basseterre)
Vance W. Amory International Airport (NEV on Nevis)
ports: Port Zante (state-of-the-art dual mega-berth cruise terminal in Basseterre)
cuisine: Stewed saltfish with spicy plantains and coconut dumplings (national dish), Goat water (spicy stew flavored with cloves, thyme, and goat meat), Cook-up rice, Conch chowder, Mangoes, Carib beer.
festivals: Sugar Mas (National Carnival in late December/January - famous for Moko Jumbies stilt walkers and Masquerade dancers)
St. Kitts Music Festival (June)
Culturama on Nevis (August)
music: Soca, Calypso, Steelband, Reggae, Iron band percussion.
dance: Moko Jumbies (towering stilt dancers), Masquerade dancers wearing peacock feather headdresses and tiny mirrors.
art: Caribelle Batik at Romney Manor (world-famous handcrafted wax batik fabrics), landscape watercolors, sea-glass art.
architecture: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park (masterpiece of British military engineering designed by slave labor); Georgian architecture around The Circus in Basseterre (modeled on Piccadilly Circus in London); plantation stone greathouses in Nevis.
literature: Caryl Phillips (acclaimed British-Kittitian novelist: Crossing the River, The Lost Child).
cinema: Filming setting for classic Caribbean travel documentaries and international features.
sports: Athletics (Kim Collins - 2003 World 100m Champion and 4-time Olympian), Cricket (Warner Park Stadium - host of World Cup and CPL matches).
media: The St. Kitts-Nevis Observer, ZIZ Broadcasting Corporation (TV/Radio), SKN Newsline.
clothing: Traditional national costume in madras plaid pattern; Moko Jumbie colorful carnival regalia.
crafts: Handcrafted wax batik fabrics from Romney Manor, woven palm hats, carved coconut shells.
worldHeritageSites: Brimstone Hill Fortress National Park (UNESCO World Heritage Site designated 1999)
unescoIntangible: Sugar Mas masquerade traditions and Moko Jumbie folklore

travelNotes: The smallest nation in the Western Hemisphere; breathtaking historic fortresses, sugar railway, and tranquil luxury in Nevis.

name: Saint Lucia
nationalAnthem: Sons and Daughters of Saint Lucia
motto: The Land, The People, The Light
majorMountains: The Pitons (Gros Piton 771 m, Petit Piton 743 m - iconic twin volcanic spires)
climate: Tropical maritime moderated by northeast trade winds; dry season December to May; wet season June to November
environmentalIssues: Coral reef protection around Soufrière Marine Management Area
biodiversity: Home to the UNESCO World Heritage Pitons Management Area, endemic Saint Lucia parrot (Jacquot), and sulfur springs
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Acting Governor-General Errol Charles)
legislature: Parliament of Saint Lucia (Senate and House of Assembly)
latestElections: General election 2021; general election scheduled 2026
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Philip J. Pierre guiding investments in youth economy, healthcare modernization (St. Jude Hospital), tourism expansion, and climate resilience.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS; maintains formal diplomatic ties with the Republic of China (Taiwan).
military: No standing army; Royal Saint Lucia Police Force (RSLPF) and Special Services Unit (SSU) / Coast Guard.
history: Inhabited by Arawak and Kalinago (Carib) peoples. Sighted by European explorers around 1500 (named for Saint Lucy of Syracuse). Long contested between Britain and France, changing flags 14 times (seven times French, seven times British), earning the nickname 'Helen of the West Indies' after Helen of Troy. Final British possession secured in 1814. Gained independence on February 22, 1979 under Sir John Compton. Remarkable for producing two Nobel Prize laureates (Sir Arthur Lewis in Economics 1979; Derek Walcott in Literature 1992)—the highest Nobel laureates per capita of any sovereign nation in the world.
recentEvents2020_2026: Achieved historic Olympic glory when Julien Alfred won Saint Lucia's first-ever Olympic medals (Gold in 100m, Silver in 200m) at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games; celebrated 45th Independence Jubilee in 2024.
historicalFigures: Sir Arthur Lewis (Nobel Memorial Prize in Economics 1979)
education: Sir Arthur Lewis Community College (SALCC in Castries) and University of the West Indies Open Campus; free basic education.
healthcare: Owen King European Union (OKEU) Hospital in Castries and St. Jude Hospital in Vieux Fort.
socialCustoms: Friday night Gros Islet street party (jump-up with seafood and sound systems), Jounen Kwéyòl (Creole Day celebrations in October), La Rose and La Marguerite flower festivals.
etiquette: Friendly and respectful, polite Creole or English greetings, modest dress away from beach resorts.
nationalIdentity: Defined by the majestic twin Piton spires, two Nobel Prize laureates, world-beating sprinting speed (Julien Alfred), and rich French-Creole cultural syncretism.
industries: Luxury resort tourism and honeymoon hospitality
Beverage brewing (Piton beer) and rum distilling
Light assembly and cardboard box packaging
agriculture: Cacao (world-renowned fine flavor chocolate estates in Soufrière)

exports: Beer and rum (Bounty rum, Chairman's Reserve)
tourism: Over 1.3 million international visitors enjoying the iconic UNESCO Pitons, Sulphur Springs (world's only drive-in volcano and mud baths), Pigeon Island National Landmark, Marigot Bay, and Jade Mountain.
employment: High employment in hotel hospitality, ecotourism guiding, public service, and agriculture.
debtInflation: XCD pegged 2.70:1 to USD; stable monetary management under ECCB.
transport: Paved coastal highway network circling the island; catamaran ferries connecting Castries and Soufrière; Express ferries to Martinique.

George F.L. Charles Airport (SLU in Castries - regional hub)
ports: Port of Castries (major Caribbean cruise and cargo hub)

Jounen Kwéyòl (Creole Day in October)
La Rose and La Marguerite Flower Festivals (August/October)
Saint Lucia Carnival (July)

unescoIntangible: La Rose and La Marguerite festival floral traditions and Kwéyòl oral heritage

coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by two Saint Lucia parrots (Jacquot), featuring a shield divided by bamboo stalks into four quarters displaying two Tudor roses and two French fleurs-de-lis, centered on a stool of African chieftaincy, topped by a torch of freedom, over the motto 'THE LAND, THE PEOPLE, THE LIGHT'.
landmarks: Sulphur Springs (Drive-in Volcano & Mineral Mud Baths)
travelNotes: The romance and adventure capital of the Caribbean; world's leading honeymoon destination; home to the breathtaking volcanic Pitons.
shortSummary: Saint Lucia is the stunning 'Helen of the West Indies', famous for the dramatic emerald volcanic spires of the Pitons rising straight from the sea, two Nobel Prize laureates, Olympic sprint champion Julien Alfred, and luxurious cocoa plantations.

name: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines
nativeName: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines / Hairoun
motto: Pax et Justitia (Peace and Justice)
climate: Tropical maritime with constant ocean trade winds; wet season June to December
naturalHazards: Active volcanic eruptions (La Soufrière erupted explosively in April 2021)
Hurricanes (Hurricane Beryl struck southern Grenadines in July 2024)
environmentalIssues: Coral reef restoration in the Grenadines
biodiversity: Volcanic main island of Saint Vincent surrounded by 32 enchanting Grenadine coral cays (Bequia, Mustique, Canouan, Mayreau, Tobago Cays Marine Park)
headOfState: King Charles III (represented by Governor-General Dame Susan Dougan)
latestElections: General election 2020; general election scheduled late 2025/2026
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Ralph Gonsalves ('Comrade Ralph') leading multi-island climate reconstruction, hospital modernization, and port expansions; served as president pro tempore of CELAC.
foreignRelations: Member of CARICOM, OECS, Commonwealth, UN, OAS, ALBA; maintains formal diplomatic ties with the Republic of China (Taiwan); historic UN Security Council non-permanent seat (2020-2021).
military: No standing army; Royal Saint Vincent and the Grenadines Police Force (RSVGPF) and Coast Guard.
history: Inhabited by the indigenous Kalinago (Caribs) who called the island Hairoun. Intermarriage with shipwrecked and escaped enslaved Africans created the Black Carib (Garifuna) people. Chief Joseph Chatoyer led the Black Caribs in the Carib Wars against British expansion in the 1770s and 1790s; following Chatoyer's death in 1795, the British forcibly exiled thousands of Garifuna to Roatán (Honduras), from where they spread across Central America. Gained independence on October 27, 1979 under Milton Cato.
recentEvents2020_2026: Rebuilt infrastructure across Union Island and Carriacou following Category 5 Hurricane Beryl in July 2024; completed Argyle International Airport solar park; chaired CELAC leaders' summits.
religions: Protestant (Anglican ~17.8%, Pentecostal ~17.6%, Methodist ~10.9%, Seventh-day Adventist ~10.2%, Baptist ~10.0%) ~75%
education: Community College of Saint Vincent and the Grenadines (SVGCC); universal secondary education.
healthcare: Milton Cato Memorial Hospital in Kingstown and modern diagnostic medical centers.
socialCustoms: Vincy Mas Carnival celebrations, sailing regattas in Bequia, sharing roasted breadfruit and fried jackfish on beach limes.
etiquette: Friendly, polite, courteous greetings, respectful demeanor in church and formal civic events.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated for the paradise islands of the Grenadines, the heroic indigenous heritage of Joseph Chatoyer, volcanic majesty, and world-class sailing.
industries: Luxury mega-yacht chartering and maritime tourism
Ship repair and boatbuilding in Bequia
naturalResources: Pristine coral cays and turquoise anchorages
energy: Over 25% renewable: Hydroelectric plants on Richmond and Colonarie rivers, solar farms, backed by modern fuel generators
tourism: Over 400,000 visitors enjoying the Tobago Cays Marine Park (crystal turquoise lagoon with green sea turtles), Bequia island charm, private luxury on Mustique, and climbing La Soufrière volcano.
employment: Tourism and yachting hospitality, smallholder agriculture, maritime seafaring, public administration.
debtInflation: XCD pegged 2.70:1 to USD; fiscal support bolstered by multilateral climate reconstruction grants.
transport: Windward and Leeward coastal highways; regular passenger ferries connecting Kingstown to Bequia, Canouan, Mayreau, and Union Island.
airports: Argyle International Airport (SVD on St. Vincent - modern gateway handling international widebody jets)
cuisine: Roasted breadfruit and fried jackfish (national dish: fire-roasted breadfruit served with crispy seasoned jackfish and pepper sauce), Callaloo soup, Ducana, Madongo dumplings (made from arrowroot), Curried conch, Hairoun beer.
festivals: Vincy Mas (National Carnival in June/July - famous for Wet Fete and Soca Monarch)
Bequia Easter Regatta (world-famous traditional boat racing)
Nine Mornings Festival (unique Vincentian Christmas tradition celebrated nine mornings before Christmas with early morning street parades)
music: Soca (Skinny Fabulous, Kevin Lyttle - global hit 'Turn Me On'), Calypso, Steelband, Reggae.
dance: Vincy Mas carnival wine, traditional quadrille and John Canoe folk dances.
art: Traditional woodcarvings, model schooner building in Bequia, sea-glass jewelry, landscape oils.
architecture: Cobblestone and brick colonial arcades in Kingstown ('City of Arches'); St. George's Anglican Cathedral; historic wooden cottages in Bequia.
literature: Shake Keane (renowned jazz trumpeter and pioneering vernacular poet: One Week Deep), Ellsworth McGranahan 'Shake' Keane.
cinema: Filming setting for Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl (filmed at Wallilabou Bay, where set ruins remain).
sports: Cricket (Arnos Vale Stadium - historic venue for international test matches and 2024 T20 World Cup), Football (Vincy Heat), Netball.
media: The Vincentian, Searchlight, SVG TV, NBC Radio SVG.
clothing: Traditional national costume in blue, gold, and green; breezy sailing apparel; Vincy Mas carnival costumes.
crafts: Handmade model whaleboats and schooners in Bequia, woven straw mats and baskets, arrowroot flour packaging.
worldHeritageSites: Tentative List: Rock Art of St. Vincent, Grenadines Island Group, La Soufrière National Park
unescoIntangible: Nine Mornings festival tradition and Vincy Mas steelpan heritage
flagDescription: Vertical tricolor of cobalt blue, yellow (double width), and green, with three green diamonds arranged in a 'V' shape (symbolizing Vincent and the 'Gems of the Antilles') centered on the yellow stripe.
coatOfArmsDescription: Features two women in classical Roman dress: one holding an olive branch, the other kneeling before a flaming altar, topped by a cotton plant, with motto 'PAX ET JUSTITIA'.
landmarks: Wallilabou Bay (Pirates of the Caribbean film set)
St. Vincent Botanic Gardens (founded 1765 - oldest botanical garden in the Western Hemisphere)
travelNotes: The premier sailing and island-hopping archipelago in the Caribbean; swimming with sea turtles in Tobago Cays.
shortSummary: Saint Vincent and the Grenadines is an enchanting constellation of 32 islands and cays in the southern Caribbean, renowned for the emerald waters of Tobago Cays, historic sailing schoneers, the active volcano of La Soufrière, and the unique Nine Mornings festival.

name: Trinidad and Tobago
nationalAnthem: Forged from the Love of Liberty
motto: Together We Aspire, Together We Achieve
highestPoint: El Cerro del Aripo (940 m on Trinidad)
longestRiver: Caroni River (40 km) / Ortoire River (50 km)
majorLakes: Pitch Lake (world's largest natural deposit of asphalt / pitch)
majorMountains: Northern Range (El Cerro del Aripo, El Tucuche)
Main Ridge on Tobago (oldest legally protected rainforest reserve in the world, est. 1776)
climate: Tropical maritime with dry season (January to May) and wet season (June to December); situated safely south of primary hurricane path
naturalHazards: Localized tropical flooding and landslides during rainy season
biodiversity: Highest bird biodiversity in the insular Caribbean (over 470 species), Caroni Bird Sanctuary (scarlet ibises), and leatherback sea turtle nesting beaches in Grande Riviere
legislature: Parliament of Trinidad and Tobago (Senate and House of Representatives)
latestElections: General election 2020; local government 2023; general election scheduled 2025
politicalSituation: Prime Minister Dr. Keith Rowley guiding deepwater energy joint ventures (Dragon gas field agreement with Venezuela), clean hydrogen development, and manufacturing diversification.
foreignRelations: Founding member of CARICOM; member of Commonwealth, UN, OAS; leading industrial, petrochemical, and diplomatic anchor of the Caribbean.
military: Trinidad and Tobago Defence Force (TTDF: Trinidad and Tobago Regiment, Coast Guard, Air Guard, Defence Force Reserves).
adminDivisions: 9 regions, 3 boroughs, 2 cities on Trinidad, and the semi-autonomous Tobago House of Assembly (THA)
history: Inhabited by Arawak and Carib peoples. Columbus sighted the three peaks of the Southern Range in 1498, naming it La Trinidad. French Catholic planters settled under the 1783 Cédula de Población. British seized Trinidad in 1797; Tobago changed colonial hands 33 times before being united with Trinidad in 1889. Following the 1834 abolition of slavery, over 147,000 indentured laborers from India arrived between 1845 and 1917, creating Trinidad's profound Indo-Caribbean cultural foundation. Gained independence on August 31, 1962 under Dr. Eric Williams (celebrated historian and founding prime minister), and became a republic in 1976.
recentEvents2020_2026: Secured US license and bilateral treaty for cross-border natural gas development in the Dragon gas field; declared the Steelpan the official National Musical Instrument in landmark 2024 legislation; advanced industrial green ammonia production.
historicalFigures: Dr. Eric Williams (Father of the Nation and author of Capitalism and Slavery)
Sir V.S. Naipaul (Nobel Prize in Literature 2001)
religions: Christianity (Roman Catholic ~21.6%, Pentecostal ~12.0%, Anglican ~5.7%, Seventh-day Adventist ~4.1%) ~55%
education: University of the West Indies (UWI) St. Augustine Campus, University of Trinidad and Tobago (UTT); free universal primary and secondary schooling.
healthcare: Eric Williams Medical Sciences Complex (Mount Hope) and Port of Spain General Hospital provide advanced tertiary care.
socialCustoms: Playing Carnival mas (world's greatest street party), enjoying 'doubles' from street vendors at breakfast, steelpan panyard rehearsals, Divali lightings.
etiquette: Lively, witty, respectful conversation ('liming'), warm hospitality, addressing elders with courtesy.
nationalIdentity: Celebrated worldwide as the birthplace of the Steelpan (the only acoustic musical instrument invented in the 20th century), Calypso, Soca, and Carnival.
sectors: Energy & Petrochemicals 45%, Services & Banking 40%, Manufacturing 10%, Agriculture 5%
industries: Liquefied Natural Gas (LNG - Atlantic LNG in Point Fortin)
Ammonia and methanol production (world's top exporter)
Petroleum refining and petrochemicals (Point Lisas Industrial Estate)
agriculture: Fine flavor Trinitario cacao (invented in Trinidad, highly prized by global chocolatiers)
Vegetables and hot peppers (Trinidad Moruga Scorpion - one of the world's hottest peppers)
naturalResources: Pitch Lake (largest natural asphalt lake on Earth)
energy: Over 99% electricity generated from domestic clean-burning natural gas; developing green hydrogen and solar energy
tourism: Over 450,000 visitors enjoying the world-famous Trinidad Carnival in Port of Spain, pristine diving at Pigeon Point and Buccoo Reef in Tobago, and Caroni Bird Sanctuary.
employment: High technical employment in petrochemical engineering, logistics, banking, and public administration.
debtInflation: Macroeconomic stability backed by the Heritage and Stabilization Fund (sovereign wealth fund); managed float currency.
transport: Uriah Butler Highway and Solomon Hochoy Highway; high-speed water taxis between Port of Spain and San Fernando; fast ferries to Tobago.
airports: Piarco International Airport (POS in Port of Spain - award-winning Caribbean airport, hub of Caribbean Airlines)
ports: Point Lisas Port (dedicated world-class industrial chemical port)
cuisine: Doubles (national street-food obsession: two fried flatbreads / bara filled with curried chickpeas / channa, topped with mango, tamarind, cucumber, and pepper sauces), Roti (buss up shut / paratha and dhalpuri with curried chicken, goat, or channa and aloo), Callaloo, Bake and shark (famous at Maracas Beach), Pelau, Crab and dumpling (Tobago specialty), Kurma, Pholourie.

Divali (public holiday with thousands of deya clay lamps)
Hosay (commemoration festival)
Eid al-Fitr
Tobago Heritage Festival

sports: Cricket (Queen's Park Oval; home to legendary Brian Lara - record holder for highest individual test score 400 not out and first-class 501 not out), Athletics (Hasely Crawford - Olympic Gold 100m 1976; Keshorn Walcott - Olympic Gold javelin 2012; Jereem Richards), Football (historic 2006 FIFA World Cup appearance).
media: Trinidad and Tobago Guardian, Trinidad Express, Newsday, CNC3, CCN TV6, TTT.
clothing: Vibrant beaded and feathered Carnival costumes; Indian ethnic attire (sari, kurta) during Divali; business casual attire.

coatOfArmsDescription: Supported by a Scarlet Ibis and a Cocrico bird, displaying Columbus's three ships (Niña, Pinta, Santa María) and two hummingbirds, topped by a golden helmet and ship's steering wheel, over the motto 'TOGETHER WE ASPIRE, TOGETHER WE ACHIEVE'.

flagDescription: The Stars and Stripes (Old Glory): 13 horizontal stripes alternating red (seven) and white (six), representing the original 13 colonies; in the canton is a blue rectangle bearing 50 white five-pointed stars representing the 50 states.
coatOfArmsDescription: The Great Seal of the United States: a bald eagle with wings displayed, holding an olive branch (with 13 leaves and 13 olives) in its right talon and a bundle of 13 arrows in its left, bearing a shield with 13 vertical red and white stripes beneath a blue chief, holding in its beak a scroll with the motto 'E PLURIBUS UNUM', surmounted by a glory of 13 stars forming a constellation.
travelNotes: Vast, diverse continental nation; iconic national park wilderness; world-class metropolitan cultural hubs; ESTA or tourist visa required.
shortSummary: The United States of America is the world's leading economic and technological superpower, celebrated for its 250-year democratic constitution, the majestic expanse of the Grand Canyon and Yellowstone, the global cultural impact of Hollywood, jazz, and rock 'n' roll, and pioneering frontiers from the Moon to artificial intelligence.
